001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.name: Garden Mosque
001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.holder: Baden-Württemberg Castles and Gardens, State Agency for Property Assets and Construction
001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.dates: The mosque complex comprises a cloister-like colonnade in the east (1779–84) and a main building (1782–86) flanked by two minarets (1786–95) in the west
001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.author: Hartmut Troll
001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.history:
The mosque in the Schwetzingen palace gardens today is the last surviving example of a type of building quite common in European landscape gardens up to the end of the 18th-century.  
The mosque, built 1782–95 by Nicolas de Pigage, was preceded by the Ambulatory, designed inside a Turkish Garden, which was first mentioned in 1774. Work on the actual mosque building started after Elector Carl Theodor had moved to Munich. The Ambulatory itself already represents contemporaneous ideas of what a mosque building looked like; the similarities with the feature of the holy sites of Mecca, published by Fischer von Erlach, are as unmistakable as the similarity of the corner pavilions with the mosque built by Chambers at Kew Gardens. The mosque itself is a fairly autonomous structure with a temple-like portico and Baroque dome.
001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.keywords: Garden Building; Turkish garden; Arabic inscriptions; minarets; Mosque; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
001f116f-84e2-522a-b67a-25d887e4cb0a.description2: The mosque is surrounded by a “Turkish garden” with winding paths and exotic plants. The architectural feature of the central building provides an original variation on the language of shapes found in baroque churches. Quotations from the western architectural history are combined with oriental motifs and inscriptions from the Qur'an. The minarets are positioned slightly in front of the western façade. The colonnade walkway with its rectangular layout is comprised of latticework open on all sides. The octagonal pavilions are decorated with dictums in Arabic and German. One striking feature is the refined roofscape with different basic slatecovered shapes, adorned by innumerable gilded crescents. The mosque’s interior is comprised of a round central hall, richly and colourfully decorated. Various general maxims are inscribed in Arabic and translated into German. These texts are not religious in nature, but generally invoke virtues, such as wisdom, diligence and discretion.

025b84b0-d00d-5c21-a749-98f3596f9d77.name: Boots
025b84b0-d00d-5c21-a749-98f3596f9d77.description: Men’s leather riding boots. The applications of leather in different colours, with representation of geometric patterns, follow the customs and superstitions of the Hausa. The Hausa possessed, in every community, workshops for producing and dyeing articles of leather, though the most out-standing locations are those of Kano and Sokoto in Nigeria; places producing, since the medieval times, the thinnest skins used in Europe. The skins are those of goat, preferably of the males, and the dye receives the local name of *bagaruwa*. This product is usually processed by women, and it is also used for treating dysentery. The products of the Hausa are distributed, by trade, across wide zones of the Sahel and Subsaharian Africa.

057cb072-73f1-5597-b0c3-f4145e5d0880.description2: Robertson's photographs of the Crimean War represent an important chapter in his career. The Crimean War was the first war in history to be extensively covered by press correspondents. The photographs taken by James Robertson and Roger Fenton put them in the ranks of the world’s first war photojournalists. James Robertson’s first photographs related to the Crimean War were actually taken in Istanbul. After England’s declaration of war on 27 March 1854, British and colonial forces dispatched to the front by sea began gathering at Selimiye in Üsküdar and neighbouring districts in April and May.

06623ef3-6331-5463-b5c0-79f3249d4f5d.description2: This oil on canvas portrait by the Swiss artist Charles Gleyre (1806–1874) depicts Ahmed Pacha Bey, the ruling prince of Tunisia at the time (1837–1855). He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold strip and a black overcoat with gold epaulets, and is wearing the *muchir*'s insignia round his neck, and the Ordre du Sang, the Nichan al-Dam, and the Grand Croix de la Légion d'Honneur medals on the left of his chest. His torso his divided in two by a shimmering red sash of honour, his black and gold sword hangs off his belt on the left-hand side, and he is wearing a red chechia on his head. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

091c2bb3-6009-5f5c-bff2-8e5c54938f6c.description2: The slightly confusing title of this print by David Roberts actually refers to the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, first commissioned in 327 AD by the Emperor Constantine and his mother Helena. at the spot where it is believed Jesus was born. The view captures the area before the iconostasis shielding the main altar in the eastern apse of the church, as well as - below on the right - the south-eastern entrance to the Grotto of the Nativity.The Church of the Nativity is one of the foremost pilgrimage sites for Christians and would have been a highlight on the itinerary of European travellers to the Holy Land. As is typical for his works, Roberts exaggerates the proportions of the architecture in relation to the human figures, which appear dwarfed by the majesty and monumentality of the structures that surround them.

0a0e3c68-6be2-5140-b568-bf800fe28f33.description2: This print was originally published in 'La Ilustracion Espanola y Americana', a newspaper published in Madrid on the 15th of April, 1882. Entitled 'La Peregrinacion religiosa de los mahometanos: Vista general de la Meca, del patio y claustro de la mesquita El-Haram y de la Santa Kaaba', it was copied from the first known photograph (at the time) depicting the Makkah precinct, taken - according to the newspaper - by the English traveller Mr [John Fryer Thomas] Keane.  Keane (1854-1937) was a clergyman, who converted to Islam and visited Makkah in 1877. In 1881, he published two books about his experiences in the Hijaz, 'Six Months in Meccah' and 'My Journey to Medinah'. The image shows the courtyard of the Makkah mosque with hundreds of pilgrims clustering around the Ka'bah at the centre. Beyond, the hills of Makkah with their traditional houses, many of them multistoreyed, can be seen.

0a226934-adb7-5611-ac1e-769b4276935b.name: *Mount Tabor*
0a226934-adb7-5611-ac1e-769b4276935b.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
0a226934-adb7-5611-ac1e-769b4276935b.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
0a226934-adb7-5611-ac1e-769b4276935b.description2: This depiction of Mount Tabor by the American artist John Douglas Woodward carries the caption 'Mount Tabor. Bearing among the Arabs, like so many other mountains, only the general name 'Jebel et Tur'. The scene suggests a rugged, primeval landscape untouched by modern humanity, the mystically lit, driven clouds that half veil the mounting evoking a spiritual and at the same time awe-inspiring atmosphere well suited to an important biblical site. In popular Christian tradition: Mount Tabor was associated with the Transfiguration of Christ. At the same time the mountain was to prove of historical importance, too.  In 1799, during the time of Napoleon Bonaparte's expedition in the area, the valley between Mount Tabor and the Moreh Hill saw a decisive battle in which a French force of about 3,000 soldiers under the command of Napoleon and General Jean Baptiste Kléber faced a Mamluk force of about 20,000 soldiers.

0c3d95fc-e6dc-5e76-8a44-96775f35c8c3.description: Both the interior and exterior of the hotel are excellent examples Zahle's traditional stone architecture. It is one of the largest and most luxurious hotels in the city, and is frequently used by officials and dignitaries.
0c3d95fc-e6dc-5e76-8a44-96775f35c8c3.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
0c3d95fc-e6dc-5e76-8a44-96775f35c8c3.history: The Kadri Hotel was built in 1906, and has borne witness to much of the violence and turmoil in modern Lebanon. The hotel was taken over by the Ottoman army in 1914, who used it is a headquarters and hospital during World War I. It was later occupied by Syrian troops and sustained enormous damage. It was restored to its former glory following an extensive restoration project in the mid 90s. The hotel was briefly closed between February 2011 and 2013.

10c5da68-3de4-54d1-9e73-5196e05c7ae8.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
10c5da68-3de4-54d1-9e73-5196e05c7ae8.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

138b0748-bba7-544a-afa4-6e44661538d4.name: *View of Constantinople*
138b0748-bba7-544a-afa4-6e44661538d4.author: Papastratos 1990, vol. 2, 578-79, figs. 617-18; Delivorrias, Fotopoulos 1997, 508-9, figs. 900-901
138b0748-bba7-544a-afa4-6e44661538d4.description2: Both this print and the *View of Smyrna* are based on earlier Western ones, which have been assimilated into the distinctive Athonite topographical style. They are exceptions to the corpus of Athonite prints, since they are of secular subjects. The printmaker was, indeed, active outside Athos, where he executed nonreligious commissions. The subjects relate to the tradition of topographical murals depicting important commercial and cultural centers of the day that decorated the mansions of wealthy merchants by the mid-eighteenth century. Kaldis aimed to supply a wider public with inexpensive works of a decorative nature. The activity of merchants from Lesbos at Smyrna, Constantinople, and the Black Sea on the one hand justified the choice of subject and, on the other, provided the appropriate network in which the multiple printed works could circulate. In order to attract the largest possible clientele, the view is coloured and annotated with explanatory comments in Greek and Turkish.

14763417-a183-5949-ac5d-11f296d400e1.description2: This hanging of red, yellow-golden and green silk is richly embroidered with silver and silver-gilt inscriptions and designs. Above, a lamp with invocations to Allah as the Opener or Judge (ya Fattah) appears suspended from an arched niche resting on two columns. Its spandrels display two roundels with the Islamic profession of Faith (shahada). Below, a quote from chapter 2 (Al-Baqarah), verse 197 of the Holy Qur’an appears: ‘…and the best provision is Al-Taqwa (piety, righteousness)’. In the lower half of the hanging, four roundels with the names of the rightly-guided caliphs surround the imperial Ottoman emblem or tughra of the sultan Abd al- Hamid II  (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD), who commissioned this curtain.. Hangings like this one may have been intended for the prayer niche of the Prophet’s mosque, as earlier examples of this type often include the inscription ‘this is the mihrab of the Prophet (pbuh)’.

171ffd50-c8dd-51b6-8ca7-e79ffd9de227.name: *The tourist's travelling equipment*
171ffd50-c8dd-51b6-8ca7-e79ffd9de227.description2: The rise of tourism saw the production of clothes and items suitable for varying climactic conditions, physical activity, and even potential dangers. This poster foregrounds an image of a hiker in an alpine setting, framed by depictions of many other types of tourism, such as seaside resorts and other more adventurous activities.

184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.name: Amelia del Valle y Serrano
184eef10-6e1e-5cd3-9d3c-79a146221593.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo (politician, historian, and collector of art and antiques) and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicate and quiet, with outstanding deep chocolate colour which reveals the quality of the photographic technique and the good condition of the object.

1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.name: The gardens of Regaleira
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.history: This Romantic estate formerly belonging to the Viscondessa of Regaleira, was acquired and enlarged by António Augusto Carvalho Monteiro (1848–1920) as his favourite country estate. His vast fortune earned him the nickname of Monteiro dos Milhões, (Moneybags Monteiro). He was inspired by the Garden of the Desert de Retz in Marly; Torrigiani Garden in Florence amongst others.
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.keywords: Neomanueline; Romanticism; Nature; Garden; Spirituality; Mistery; Alchemy
1867f5d4-3b17-57ea-bb1b-bff0861448b8.description2:
As an image of the Cosmos, the gardens of Regaleira are revealed to the visitors through the sucession of magic and mysterious places. A Paradise Lost coexists in these scenographic representations with a mundus inferus – a Dantesque underground world – through which the candidate is guided by his intuition. The various scenes offer a concrete representation of an initiation journey, like a pilgrimage through a symbolic garden in which one can feel the Harmony of the Spheres and the vertical alignment of the consciousness, in analogy with the Quest for the Supreme Being found in the great Epics.  
References abound in these realms to the worlds of classical mythology, to Virgil, Dante, Milton and Camões, to the Templar-like mission of the Order of Christ and to the enigmas of the alchemical Ars Magna.

1b1e3ef8-5e29-5178-ac83-8c4cb0d8ce8c.description: Sultan Fuad I’s letter was sent to Sorolla by Garcia Herreros. It is an invitation to spend one year with his family in the palaces of Cairo, where the painter could reside and work freely. All this is part of the artistic policy that was intended to attract well-known Western artists to the Egyptian sultan's court. Unfortunately, Sorolla was never able to take this trip, but from a letter to his wife we know the excitement that was caused by the idea of spending time in Egypt.

1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.artist: Artist: Filippo Liardo; illustrator: Gustave Janet
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.keywords: Archaeological excavations; Egyptomania; Egypt; World fairs
1bb390d7-8753-553f-9174-6119a0f96ab1.description2: Visitors to the 1867 Exposition Universelle (world fair) had the opportunity to explore a reconstruction of the Temple of Edfu in a "Parc Égyptien". This reconstruction (containing a mix of various different temples) was a response both to the fashion for ancient Egypt, and the desire for good diplomatic relations with modern Egypt. Indeed, we can see the imperial couple in this photograph standing with Isma'il Pasha, the viceroy of Egypt, who had come to see the exhibition. The Temple of Edfu had just been rediscovered by the famous Egyptologist Mariette.

1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.name: Types of Cairo
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Egypt
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.description2: The historical photos, belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection, were collected by the Florentine naturalist during his travel around the world in 1865–68 on the Magenta's steam corvette, with the purpose to start diplomatic and commercial relations. The "genre" images seem to be created "ad hoc" to represent human diversity along the different ages. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum, and are very important for the history of anthropological science and history of photography. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.name: *Hebron*
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.description2: This print is based on a watercolour by David Roberts entitled 'Hebron Mosque erected over the graves of Abraham and the Patriarchs' and completed in 1835. Apparently, this in turn was based on an initial sketch made at the Mosque by a Mrs Bracebridge. According to Jewish, Christian and Muslim tradition, the sanctuary at Hebron houses the graves of Abraham, his wife Sarah and their family. To Jews, it is the second holiest site after Jerusalem. Muslims revere the site because of its associations with Abraham and view the city of Hebron as one of the sacred cities of Islam. Formerly prosperous as a glass-manufacturing centre and hajj staging post, Hebron's fortunes declined in the 19th century due to cheap glass imports and the rerouting of the hajj caravan from Damascus to Transjordan.
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; William Finden: place of birth unknown
1d9fdf68-a63f-5cd6-937f-9223edee8336.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; William Finder: London

1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.name: Berber woman (Nailiya) lying down
1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.description: The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is lying on her side like an odalisque, wearing a colourful silk dress and the rich jewels used to perform their traditional dance. The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex-tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, which in turn led to them being repudiated in their villages. Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.

1f01b620-1564-5cb2-8825-cd2a342b9728.name: *Ambassador Mohammed ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Pasha of Tangier, visits Vienna on February 14, 1783*
1f01b620-1564-5cb2-8825-cd2a342b9728.description2: This picture shows Moroccan Ambassador Mohammed ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Pasha of Tangier, at his first visit to Vienna on 14 Feb 1783. This visit of the Moroccan delegation in Vienna started the more than 200-years-long peaceful relationship between Morocco and Austria.

1fc5fe5c-fbfa-5316-9126-a887d85076f6.name: *Description de l'Arménie la Perse*
1fc5fe5c-fbfa-5316-9126-a887d85076f6.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Félix Marie Charles Texier was a French historian, architect and archaeologist. Texier published a number of significant works involving personal travels throughout Asia Minor and the Middle East. These books included descriptions and maps of ancient sites, reports of regional geography and geology and descriptions of artwork and architecture.

204250dc-0aee-5c7b-a35b-e5449a289de5.name: Dish
204250dc-0aee-5c7b-a35b-e5449a289de5.description: In the 19th century, new forms and decorative styles began to appear on dishes from Fez, which are remarkable both for the colours used and their design. This dish, decorated with two sailing boats, resembles designs seen on ceramics from Izmir in Turkey.
204250dc-0aee-5c7b-a35b-e5449a289de5.keywords: Applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; ceramic; Iznik; Ottoman influence; Ottoman art

204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.name: A Druse Bride from Lebanon
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; Druze
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.description2: The bride wears a tantur, a head ornament worn along with a white veil by the women from Antilibano. The photo belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist on his world travels in 1865 to 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum and are important for the histories of anthropological science and photography. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the 1875 foundation of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

218e138e-ef0b-539c-a7bf-bad9297c5e84.name: *Trip to Egypt*
218e138e-ef0b-539c-a7bf-bad9297c5e84.author: DGPC
218e138e-ef0b-539c-a7bf-bad9297c5e84.keywords: Photograph; trip to Egypt; Cultural education
218e138e-ef0b-539c-a7bf-bad9297c5e84.description2: Travelling abroad, particularly to Eastern countries, became a must after Napoleon’s campaigns. This photograph, taken by Prince D. Luis Filipe and handwritten by Queen D. Amélia, features the Queen’s journey to Egypt to develop the princes’ cultural and educational skills.

23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.name: The Ottoman Clock Tower
23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.history: This clock tower was built by Yussef Afimus in 1897 neara the Grand Serail to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the Ottoman sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II's coronation. It was seen as an important tower, indicating Muslim prayer time as well as making up for the absence of a public clock tower in the city, as many private foreign institutions in Beirut had built Western style clock towers in recent years. The construction of the clock tower was approved by the sultan following a letter of supplication from Beirut's governor Rashid Bey. The ceremonial laying of the first stone took place on 9 January 1897 (the anniversary of the sultan) in the presence of high officials, military representatives and members of the municipality of Beirut.
23d98ad7-7f2d-5f3d-a18a-862042cf2b0c.description2: At 25 metres tall, the Hamidiye clock tower was the tallest structure in Beirut at the time of its completion. Similar towers were consequently built in imitation in numerous other cities of the Ottoman Empire, such as Istanbul, Izmir, Izmit, Adana, Jaffa, Nablus, Acre and Tripoli. It was built using local stone: Beirut sandstone, Jounieh limestone, Damascene basalt and Deir al-Qamar red stone. The tower houses a huge bell weighing 300kg on its third floor, and a set of 125 cast iron steps leading up to it. Four miniature orientalist-style balconies adorn this floor. Above these balconies are four large clock faces imported especially from the Ottoman embassy in France.

24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.name: *The Café des Platanes*
24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.author: Dalila Orfali
24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.keywords: Orientalism; traditional city; traditional urban space; colonial city
24505a53-36c5-5b4a-9423-5215da35cb9b.description2: This famous café is located by a fountain bearing the same name, built by the Dey Hassan. From 1832 it faced the Jardin d'Essai, giving it a view of this beautiful green space in the Hamma neighbourhood. This café and its fountain were immortalised by a number of painters. Various 17th century texts recall its peaceful atmosphere.

2490e8e8-85c3-5eea-8a98-4c2d970e5157.name: Photograph of the German Emperor while on a visit to Tangier
2490e8e8-85c3-5eea-8a98-4c2d970e5157.description: This photograph was taken during German Emperor Kaiser Wilhelm II’s official visit to Tangier.
2490e8e8-85c3-5eea-8a98-4c2d970e5157.keywords: Diplomacy; photograph; visual document; international relations; European powers; German in Morocco

254ea7af-536e-5a78-8206-f0d4cc517b93.name: *Study of an Arab*
254ea7af-536e-5a78-8206-f0d4cc517b93.description2: *Study of an Arab* by Frederick Lewis, and important orientalist painter and etcher.

26e9ef4b-0b68-5435-8e38-53a259f9cdaf.name: Portrait of Prosper Enfantin dressed in an imitation of the local style
26e9ef4b-0b68-5435-8e38-53a259f9cdaf.description2: Prosper Enfantin (1796–1864) was one of the most active members of the Saint-Simonian movement (a socio-economic and political movement advocating a fraternal, socialist society based on economic prosperity). After being imprisoned in 1832 for founding a very politically-active community, Enfantin became fascinated by the Middle East, and in 1834 he left for Egypt with a few companions. He was also one of the proponents of the Suez Canal. In this image he is dressed in the local Egyptian style, wearing clothes he made himself.

275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

28f6f7de-3daa-59e6-960d-f0cac66b210d.name: North African caravan, in the west of the Sahara
28f6f7de-3daa-59e6-960d-f0cac66b210d.third_name: A Travers le Monde, Paris: Hachette, 1895–1914
28f6f7de-3daa-59e6-960d-f0cac66b210d.description2: Camille Douls (1864–1889), who was passionate  about Africa, decided in the late 19th century to enter indigenous North African territory, despite it being forbidden for foreigners at the time. He began to learn Arabic and study the Quran for this purpose, and was able to live among the Oulad Delim tribe for five months, although not without risk to his personal safety. He published his observations on his return (1888), which attracted much attention, as no European had lived among these people to date. He was assassinated the following year during a trip to Algeria. The tale of his time in the desert was illustrated by Jules Girardet, an artist specialising in historical scenes who had never seen the subjects of his drawings. This image is therefore interesting, as it sheds light on the nature of the stereotypical Western gaze on nomadic lifestyles.

28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.name: *The arrival of Suleiman Pasha, envoy of the Porte, in Giurgiu*
28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.second_name: *The arrival of the Ottoman army in Valahia*
28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.description2: In June 1848 revolution broke out in Wallachia, aiming to liberate the country from the Ottoman sovereignty. Prince Bibescu was deposed and a provisional government was installed. As a result, the sultan sent an army to Wallachia. The Ottoman army entered on the Romanian territory in July and the Porte’s representative, Suleiman Pasha, began negotiations with the Romanian revolutionary government. This chromolithograph is part of a series of German chromolithographs depicting episodes from the Revolution that took place in Wallachia in 1848. It shows the entrance of Süleyman Pasha, the Porte's envoy, accompanied by a part of his army of 20.000 soldiers, in Giurgiu, a port on the Danube, after having crossed the river. He is received by a Romanian delegation.

2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.name: Menu for the gala dinner offered by the Italian king in honour of the Ambassador from Morocco, who visited Italy in June 1890
2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.author: Giulia Barrera
2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.archival: ACS, Min. Real Casa, Uff. Prefetto di Palazzo, filza 107, f. 3 "Ambasciata marocchina. Suo arrivo e soggiorno a Roma"
2cf5398f-8d6e-5e13-b679-67442f1bcbc6.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador – who was escorted by his secretary, an interpreter, and some dignitaries – was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered a gala dinner for him.  
The menu for the gala dinner was in French. A military band played different pieces of music during the dinner.

2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.name: Beaufort Castle
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.description: The Beaufort Castle was a crusader castle located near the town of Nabatiyeh, in South Lebanon. The castle was named "Bel Fort" or "Beau Fort" by the Crusaders in the 12th century. Its name in Arabic is *Qal'at al-Shaqiif*, meaning Castle on the High Rock. The castle was also used for military purposes in the 20th century, particularly during the civil war, due to its strategic location.
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.history: In 1139, King Fulk of Jerusalem gained control of this area and begun the construction of Beaufort castle shortly afterwards. Although Saladin recaptured Beaufort in 1190, the castle was returned to crusader hands only 60 years later. In 1268 Sultan Baybars finally gained control of the fortress. However, the upper portion was destroyed by the Ottomans in the 17th century, as they sought to quash Emir Fakhr al-Din II, who had taken the castle as part of his network of fortifications. Following the Galilee Earthquake in 1837, which caused considerable damage to the structure, the castle was abandoned and its ruins were used by local farmers to shelter sheep, and as a quarry.
2e86f805-0ac2-5af3-82ca-11820cd27c1d.keywords: fortress; castle; tourism; ruins; Beaufort; medieval

30b913ab-d3b2-56b2-ac63-f81083c8e870.name: Theresian thaler
30b913ab-d3b2-56b2-ac63-f81083c8e870.keywords: Arabian Pensinsula; Maria Theresia; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics
30b913ab-d3b2-56b2-ac63-f81083c8e870.description2: The Maria Theresian Thaler, a large silver coin originally created by Queen (Empress) Maria Theresia, minted in Austria until 1890. It was used in the Arabic Peninsula as a means of payment. This coin was countersigned at the Arabian mint of Ras Bab el Mandeb in 1890.

316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.name: *Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey* (painting)
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.keywords: Oil on canvas; B. de Moynier; Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.description2: This 1861 oil on canvas by B. de Moynier shows the Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey in front of the throne in the great hall of the Palais du Bardo, his right hand on the Tunisian constitution (which he has just proclaimed), his left holding his sword. He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold stripe and a short black coat with a gold belt and epaulets, in addition to the Nichan al-Amen medal and a green sash with a double red stripe. On his chest the Nichan al-Dam, the Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (classe majeur) medals can be seen, as well as a Légion d'Honneur and Nichan al-Iftikhar on a sling. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.name: *Description of the Arab monuments of Granada, Seville and Córdoba: the Alhambra, the Alcazar and the Great Mosque*
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.description: The publications about the Spanish Muslim Antiquities, including monuments can be retraced to the end of the 18th century. Interest in these monuments is related to the interest in this unique heritage in Europe, as part of the Alhambresque and Neo-Mudéjar styles in Spain and Europe. The publication of the monument’s descriptions aided in their conservation.
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.author: Ana Cabrera
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.third_name: *Estudio descriptivo de los monumentos árabes de Granada, Sevilla y Córdoba o sea, La Alhambra, El Alcazar y la gran Mezquita de Occidente*

32e505cb-9f9d-5883-b87d-e0aff2e6436e.name: Pera Palace Hotel
32e505cb-9f9d-5883-b87d-e0aff2e6436e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
32e505cb-9f9d-5883-b87d-e0aff2e6436e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient İstanbul; hotel; travelling
32e505cb-9f9d-5883-b87d-e0aff2e6436e.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

32fb3761-3d91-5ac8-b9e9-d93cf46f8c28.name: Lamp from a mosque
32fb3761-3d91-5ac8-b9e9-d93cf46f8c28.keywords: Exploration; Aden; travel; traveller; mosque interior decoration
32fb3761-3d91-5ac8-b9e9-d93cf46f8c28.description2: This lamp from a mosque was purchased from a Yemenite from Saana by Franz Steindacher in Aden in 1896. Steindacher was part of an Austrian expedition to explore the Red Sea.

331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.name: *Aegilops ovata* L.
331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.author: Ana Isabel Correia (FCUL/MUHNAC-UL)
331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.keywords: herbarium; vascular plant; grass; goatgrass; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.materials: Pressed and dried plant, glued on paper
331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.description2: This is a Portuguese case of this scientific transnational reality. Herbarium sheet with three fruiting specimens of Aegilops ovata. The specimens were collected in Algeria, in May 1840 by the Scientific Commission of Argelia, under M. Durieu supervision. It includes a label with the scientific name and collecting details, as well as a color scale and a linear scale. A detail: Genus Aegilops is possibly one of the ancestors to common wheat.
331be2fc-32f2-5ed5-bb67-3f9817fcb2d0.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional da Historia Natural e da Ciencia (MUHNAC)

33430dbe-c0fc-5bb4-9845-6bce853a6ea6.name: General Hullin's audience, provided by the Dey of Algeria
33430dbe-c0fc-5bb4-9845-6bce853a6ea6.description2: In August 1802, irritated by the repeated pillaging of his ships by Algerian pirates, Napoléon I sent General Hullin and Consul Dubois-Thainville to the then Dey of Algeria, Mustafa Pasha, with a threatening message. This print is an example of Napoleonic propaganda, as it attempts to highlight the "insolence" of the bey, who stays seated on the sofa, and the "bravery" of the general who, with a sword on his side, makes his speech.

33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and Amelia del Valle y Serrano, in Oriental garment
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and her daughter Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicious thanks to the typical Turkish costume, the apparently easy pose and the scenography and the absolute harmony with the idea of aesthetic orientalism.
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.third_name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquesa de Cerralbo, y Amelia del Valle y Serrano, con atuendo oriental

35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.name: *The Moroccan Embassy in Rome*
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.author: Giulia Barrera
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.archival: *La Tribuna illustrata*, a. I, n. 26, 29 June 1890, p. 404
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.third_name: *L’Ambasciata marocchina a Roma (da fotografie del conte Luigi Primoli)*
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.second_name: The Sultan of Morocco’s ambassador who visited Italy in 1890 and some of his entourage (four captains, the interpreter, two servants)
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered him a gala dinner.  
In these pictures one can see (from the top left): four captains who escorted Morocco’s Ambassador, his interpreter Lamfaddal Elkabbagi, the Ambassador on a carriage arriving at the King’s palace, Hamed (one of the Ambassador’s servants), Pà Nadan (another servant), and two children travelling with the Ambassador on the hotel’s terrace.
35118a9c-ae87-5875-b6fd-694c3a29ac01.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.name: *Woman In Oriental Dress*
35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.author: Petar Petrovic
35645306-e708-561a-ae81-24e697df6d15.description2: In order to evoke and convey the spirit of the Balkans and the Orient as faithfully as possible, Paja Jovanović meticulously recorded each detail of the interior of a typical Balkan or Eastern house. He also collected props that made up a family’s inventory of furniture (e.g. the hexagonal decorative table to the left), and carefully studied the physiognomies and characters of the men and women he encountered in the southern Balkans, in Egypt, Constantinople, the Caucasus and elsewhere. The precision of draughtsmanship and freshness of colour in this painting by Paja Jovanović ranks it among his more successful works from the mid-1880s.

359a8351-850d-54e6-b825-353190856a52.name: Small vial
359a8351-850d-54e6-b825-353190856a52.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
359a8351-850d-54e6-b825-353190856a52.description2: This small hexagonal vial is decorated with arabesques, floral motifs and Arabic inscriptions, written in cartouches bordered by red copper, reading "work is beneficial, courtesy is a matter of well-being, ignorance is baseness"

3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.name: *L’escalier des lions* (painting)
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.keywords: Palais du Bardo; capitals; ceramic panels; Andalusian style
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
3684ea69-4081-5b3d-99c4-ac49b735a423.description2: This important painting depicts the official entrance of the Palais du Bardo as it was originally, with the *escalier des lions* and Mohamed Sadok Bey exiting the palace in official uniform, accompanied by Tunisian dignitaries, preceded by protocol officers and surrounded by the beylical guard. It shows the monumental *escalier des lions* with its archways and columns on the façade. We can also see its glorious white marble columns, capitals and ceramic panels decorating the walls and mounted on plaster and stucco (*naqsh hadida*). Through the entrance doors the black and white archways in an Andalusian style can be seen on the first floor.

392f3d7f-32c6-5e59-aeea-0cf54fb842cc.name: *The Victoria Nile - At Rionga's Island*
392f3d7f-32c6-5e59-aeea-0cf54fb842cc.second_name: Egypt. The Victoria Nile - exploration by canoe among the papyri
392f3d7f-32c6-5e59-aeea-0cf54fb842cc.description2: People had been trying to find the source of the Nile since antiquity. However, interest in this increased significantly in the early 19th century, and lead to various scientific observations. These observations were published and illustrated with engravings, which allowed Europeans to better understand the African continent.

39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.name: Box with the image of an artillery emplacement of the Austro-Hungarian Army at the Sinai in 1916
39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.keywords: Palestine; Bethlehem; Suez Channel; Egypt; Austrian army; war; warfare
39b49b4c-4d71-5eb2-ae22-21ea92dca300.description2: This silver box was made in memory of the Sinai Desert campaign embarked upon by soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian Army. At the end of 1915, two Austro-Hungarian artillery units were transported to reach the front at Gallipoli after a demand for support from the Ottoman Empire. In 1916, the 15cm howitzer battery was transferred to Smyrna and the mobile 24cm mortar battery was stationed near Haifa in Palestine to defend Mount Carmel. Other parts of the unit took part in the battle of Gaza and remained in the area till 1918. The last members of these Austro-Hungarian units were finally repatriated to Trieste in 1919.

39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.name: National Evangelical Church of Beirut
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.description: The National Evangelical Church of Beirut is the first native Arabic Protestant congregation in the Middle East. It acts as the headquarters and administrative centre for the nine evangelical churches which operate under the name of the National Evangelical Union of Lebanon. Today, the church organises social, cultural, and educational activities, and runs two schools in Beirut and one in the Beqaa. It is also involved with the theological education at the Near East School of Theology in Beirut.
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.history: Established in 1848 by Congregational and Presbyterian American missionaries, the National Evangelical Church of Beirut is the oldest and largest of nine congregations situated inside Beirut. The church acted as a centre for the activities and celebrations for both the English and Arabic speaking communities until it was completely destroyed during the Lebanese Civil war. The clock tower was the only aspect of the church to survive the war, and the church itself was rebuilt in 1998. Today, it is fully functioning and located in Beirut's Central District.
39c4d9ff-e32f-5e06-bea2-e9873ae36a23.keywords: church; Evangelical; tourism; site; monument; religion; Protestant

39c5d2fa-be8f-55e6-97ea-9cd4b0e30514.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
39c5d2fa-be8f-55e6-97ea-9cd4b0e30514.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.name: Seated Berber woman (Nailiya)
3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.description:
The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is sitting among rich cushions, wearing a colourful silk dress and the jewels used to perform their traditional dance.  
The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, in turn leading to being repudiated in their villages.  
Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.

3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.name: Orient Express Poster
3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

3c16e6a6-882d-588d-8f9d-b0309a8c41db.name: *The Empress' boulevard*
3c16e6a6-882d-588d-8f9d-b0309a8c41db.author: Dalila Orfali
3c16e6a6-882d-588d-8f9d-b0309a8c41db.description2: Painted in 1865, this canvas was one of many the artist created depicting "the new boulevard of Algiers". This boulevard, built by the opera house where Saint-Saëns was performing at the time, was the architect Frédéric Chassériau's (the painter's uncle) first significant work. It was inaugurated in 1839 by Napoléon III and the Empress Eugénie, after whom it it was named, and marked the beginning of Algiers' new, European-style urbanisation programme, which affected both the city and its surroundings. Although these changes did bring the city's inhabitants a number of comforts, they also resulted in the irrevocable destruction of a number of very important monuments from the Ottoman era.

3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.name: *An Elephant*; *An indian Ox*; *An Antelope*
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.author: Marina Minozzi
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist painting; Italian painters; exoticism; artistic exchanges; France; international exhibitions; universal exposition; travel; imaginary trips; travelling artist; natural sciences
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.description2: In 1891 Filippo Palizzi donated more than 300 paintings to the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in order to describe his entire career through his artworks. All of them are cited in the Chronological List of 1853, which includes 12 studies depicting exotic animals done in The Jardin des Plantes in Paris. The series is considered the preparatory base for the amazing painting *Dopo il Diluvio. Uscita degli animali dall’Arca* (*After the Flood. The Animals Exiting the Ark*), commissioned by King Vittorio Emanuele II for the Museum of Capodimonte and presented in 1867 at the Universal Exposition in Paris. Other animals, like the Indian ox, the antelope and the dromedary were depicted in the Jardin des Plantes in Paris with the same aim.
3c3428ad-e6d9-50dc-93c0-7e7ab1c900d2.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Di Majo, E., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. 5.24; cat. 5.63; cat. 5.64.

3c81118b-d41d-514c-bb93-87850f2cc0d1.name: *The City of Algiers from the Sea*
3c81118b-d41d-514c-bb93-87850f2cc0d1.author: Houria Cherid
3c81118b-d41d-514c-bb93-87850f2cc0d1.third_name: *The City of Algiers from the Sea*
3c81118b-d41d-514c-bb93-87850f2cc0d1.description2: A lithograph depicting Algiers, as seen from the sea.

3d0846e1-bd02-5620-aaab-623dc4af1ff9.name: Photo documenting the discovery of the Tutankhamun tomb
3d0846e1-bd02-5620-aaab-623dc4af1ff9.description2: The Tomb of Tutankhamun was discovered in 1922 in the Valley of the Kings by Egyptologist Howard Carter. The discovery of this tomb caused a wide media stir worldwide.

3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.name: *The Great Mosque of Algiers*
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.author: Dalila Orfali
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.keywords: Old Algiers; traditional urban space; colonial city; Orientalism
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.description2: This painting was the first of Sintès' works to be bought by the museum on its opening in 1930. In actual fact it does not depict the mosque known as the "Great Mosque", but rather the "Djemâa ed-Djedid" (Jama'a al-Jadid) built in the 17th century in the style of the Turkish mosques from the city of Bursa. Here, the mosque appears overlooking the city's seafront ramparts, whilst the port neighbourhood's urban development does not appear to have begun.

3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.name: *A Coffee House in Tophane*
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.keywords: Thomas Allom; Jivanian; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.description2: A Thomas Allom composition which appears in the first volume of Robert Walsh’s book *Constantinople and Scenery of Seven Churches of Asia Minor* is *The Coffee-House*. This is an oil copy of the composition by Civanyan. Written by Robert Walsh, who served as the private priest of British ambassador Lord Strangford after 1820, the book was published in two volumes in London in 1838. It includes engravings and the book, which was later published in French, acted as an important visual resource on Istanbul and its engravings were used as models by numerous artists. In the corresponding text, Robert Walsh provides information on the interior organisation and decoration of the coffeehouse and relates various details ranging from making music and smoking pipes to the plays of the *meddah* (storytellers).

40e07960-2c59-5c21-8ff8-0aa9645bf0eb.name: Postcards showing Romanian tourists in Egypt
40e07960-2c59-5c21-8ff8-0aa9645bf0eb.description2: In the 19th century, North Africa was mostly known to Romanians from geography schoolbooks and newspaper articles. However, starting from the middle of the 19th century there are information about wealthy Romanians who visited North African countries, some of them recounting in their memoirs their African experiences. For example, Romanian poet and politician Vasile Alecsandri visited in September-October 1853 the Moroccan ports of Tangier and Tétouan and published his impressions in a Romanian literary periodical. A bit more than half a century later, four Romanian students entered an international competition for travelling by foot 100,000 km. In July 1911 they reached Egypt, where they visited Cairo, the pyramids, the Valley of the Kings, Memphis, Luxor, Karnak, Aswan, the Abu Simbel temples.

40f40e78-356d-5bdf-a281-3045eb71b83b.name: Hammam-el-Lif, Tunis. Seaside resorts and thermal springs
40f40e78-356d-5bdf-a281-3045eb71b83b.description2: Hammam el-Lif is a seaside town near Tunis. In 1750, Ali II Bey of Tunis had a pavilion built by the thermal springs, which Hussein II Bey then completed in 1826.

41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.name: Portrait of Archduke Maximilian
41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.description2: Portrait of the Archduke Ferdinand Maximilian, who was commander of the Austrian Navy. In 1855 he visited parts of the Ottoman Empire including Smyrna, Palestine and Egypt.

427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.name: The Hotel Excelsior at the Lido in Venice at the end of construction work
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.holder: Archivio Progetti – Università Iuav di Venezia
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.author: Riccardo Domenichini
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.description2: The photograph shows the Hotel Excelsior on the beach of the Lido sandbar which separates the Venice lagoon from the sea. The building appears to be almost finished but not yet open: since the hotel was inaugurated in 1908, the photograph was probably shot before then. Giovanni Sardi was one of the most gifted architects of the eclectic generation. Here, he uses elements of the Moorish architecture like minarets and domes mixed with decorations in the Art Nouveau style and medieval elements, to emphasize the character of the building as a fabulous place for holidays and amusement.

441fd91e-6a8d-5ba0-b0fb-73ae59155d8a.name: *Voyage Dans Le Levant*
441fd91e-6a8d-5ba0-b0fb-73ae59155d8a.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

454ea471-63b6-545e-9c35-ea8207b4746b.name: *General View of the Erecteion* (Athens)
454ea471-63b6-545e-9c35-ea8207b4746b.description: View of the Erecteion in Athens. The drawing is part of the documentation of different monuments during the trip in the Arapiles frigate to Near East.
454ea471-63b6-545e-9c35-ea8207b4746b.keywords: Exploration; Early European collection; Travelling; Greece

45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.name: *Exposition d’Art Musulman*
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.author: Mina Moraitou
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.keywords: photo; Egypt; Greeks; Iznik; collecting; exhibition
45cab7c7-4fad-588f-ae17-e78354e7fd67.description2: A photo depicting a showcase with Iznik ceramics belonging to Greek and European collectors such as Benakis, Nomico, Lagonico and Salvago. Many of the works were collected by Greeks in Egypt and were included in the *Exposition d’Art Musulman*, organised by Gaston Migeon and held in Alexandria in 1925 while a number more were shown in the earlier great Islamic exhibition in Munich in 1910.

460ebced-3992-593a-a42e-32453e973f11.name: *Mountain people from Mostaganem*
460ebced-3992-593a-a42e-32453e973f11.author: Dalila Orfali
460ebced-3992-593a-a42e-32453e973f11.description2: The subjects of this piece, drawn from life, are men from the west of Algeria. Although we know that Chassériau's main source of inspiration in Algeria was the city of Constantine, he also spent some time in Algiers with his uncle the architect Frédéric Chassériau, who had been employed by Napoléon III to build up the city's seafront. The artist's keen attention to detail is highlighted by his authentic rendition of his subjects' dress and his occasional use of Arabic in his annotations.

47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.name: *Hagia Sophia. General view*
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.description: Photographic print that is part of an album of different Istanbul images taken by the studio of the three Armenian brothers who, in 1880, opened a headquarters in this city. It shows the central nave of the Mosque of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya Camii), under the main dome, facing the Eastern apse where the altar has been replaced by a *mihrab*. On the left, in the transept, the pavilion for the sultan's personal prayer. A group of men are sitting on the ground, on carpets that cover the entire surface, listening attentively. This kind of album had great success with 19th century European travellers.
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.author: Rebeca C. Recio

47bb854c-9eb2-5d07-b0f1-7d41e63b0500.name: *The Qadous path*
47bb854c-9eb2-5d07-b0f1-7d41e63b0500.author: Dalila Orfali
47bb854c-9eb2-5d07-b0f1-7d41e63b0500.description2: The clever use of light in this painting helps illustrate the beauty of the countryside around Algiers in the 19th century. It highlights the richness of the vegetation in the area surrounding the Algerian notability's country homes.

483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.name: *Dala’il al-Khayrat* (*Guidelines to Blessings*) by Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jazuli)
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.dimensions: 164 mm x 224 mm (open); 164 mm x 112 mm (closed)
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
483e8679-d93d-56cd-b566-f321c598b6de.description2: The *Dala’il al-Khairat* (The Signs of Benediction) is a compilation of prayers for the Prophet Muhammad and other faith-related information by Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jazuli (d. ca. 1465). Popular throughout the Muslim world and particularly in Ottoman lands. It also contains descriptions of the Holy Mosque in Makkah and the Prophet’s Mosque in Madina, the two most important Islamic pilgrimage sites. Both are typically depicted in the centre of the manuscript, Here, detailed birds-eye views of both sanctuaries appear, surrounded by gold margins. On the right, at tthe heart of the Makkah mosque, the Ka’bah is dressed with its black kiswa cover, further enhanced by a golden belt (hizam) above and a golden door curtain (sitara or burqu’). On the left, within the mosque complex at Madina, a domed chamber contains the tombs of the Prophet and the first caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar, draped in golden covers – perhaps a reference to the precious, gold and silver-embroidered textiles that were spread over the tombs in Ottoman times.

48ea8829-906b-5b5c-b95e-df1cb62f4107.name: Delacroix's journal (volume 1)
48ea8829-906b-5b5c-b95e-df1cb62f4107.author: Dalila Orfali
48ea8829-906b-5b5c-b95e-df1cb62f4107.artist: Delacroix, E., Flat, P., Piot, R.
48ea8829-906b-5b5c-b95e-df1cb62f4107.archival: Delacroix, E., Flat, P. and Piot, R., *Journal de Eugène Delacroix*, Paris, Plon, Nourrit et Cie., 1893
48ea8829-906b-5b5c-b95e-df1cb62f4107.description2: The library at the Musée National des Beaux-Arts holds 9,000 works on the history of universal art, resting on shelves designed by the Artist Louis Fernez (1900–1984). The 19th century collection contains a series of books on the history of Algeria, including three volumes from the *Journal de Eugène Delacroix*, written during his time in Oran and Algiers in 1832, as well as two books by Fromentin.

48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.name: Repairing pyramids road, Cairo
48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.description2: The Pyramids Road was fully repaired and put into use in 1868, successfully joining Giza to Cairo. Thanks to rising tourism in the area, different modes of transport were introduced along this route: cabs and omnibuses in the 19th century, and a tramway in the 20th century. The road was finally resurfaced following the invention of the motorcar, as we can see in this photograph.

490493f4-f4d8-56c4-8bdc-7207e915de8b.name: Travels in the Read Sea. *The Temple of Medina*
490493f4-f4d8-56c4-8bdc-7207e915de8b.keywords: Travelling; Egypt; Red sea; religious buildings
490493f4-f4d8-56c4-8bdc-7207e915de8b.description2: *L'Illustration* was a weekly French magazine published between 1834 and 1944. The greatest artists and photographers were featured in its pages, which dealt mainly with current affairs, and offered a great variety of information to the French public. Pictured here is a view of the mosque of Medina and the many pilgrims who had travelled there.

4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.name: A photograph of the Wall of al-Buraq (also known as The Western Wall or Wailing Wall)
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.archival: Johnstone, Catherine Laura, *Christian and Jewish Pilgrims to the Holy Land*, London, 1899
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community
4a68de52-6e31-5b77-857c-17466cc31f3c.description2: This photograph shows the Wall of a-Buraq/Western Wall as it appeared in 1899. As well as being interested in the Christian holy places in Palestine, many European pilgrims were curious about other meaningful places and the life and habits of the Jewish communities in Palestine. The Wailing Place, as it was called in the caption of the photograph, was seen by many European (Christian) pilgrims not only in relation to historical events but as specifically related to the increasing presence of Jews coming from Europe to Palestine towards the end of the 19th century. Whether describing local Muslims and Jews or the European Jews, many European travellers associated Muslims and Jews with the “exotic” and with “otherness” in their appearance and habits.

4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.name: *Interior of a house in Boussaada*
4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.author: Dalila Orfali
4bccb3e9-a964-52ef-937f-7a6d6e11e5cf.description2: This painting, showing the interior of a traditional house in the Boussaada region, elicits a certain intimacy, recalling the muted atmosphere also evoked by Guillaumet's *Fileuse*. The nervous, moving brushstrokes and his use of melted or soldered lead are clear references to the style of the Dutch masters.

4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.name: Map of the Network of Caravans
4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.keywords: Egypt; North Eastern Africa; Western Arabia; Caravans
4c695d43-f03d-5a2c-8f4d-af48b299d76b.description2: This sketch shows the network of caravans in Egypt, North Eastern Africa and Western Arabia.

4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.name: *The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia, Volume 1, title page*
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.description2: This vignette depicts the façade of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, located on the spot where it is bellieved both the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his burial took place. David Roberts, the prominent Scottish Orientalist painter(1796-1864) visited at Easter time, when the square in front of the church was crowded with pilgrims and traders selling their wares. Nevertheless, he shows the scene not with contemporary life milling around the church, but enlivened only with his usual repertoire of carefully staged, oriental types. Originally, the church was accessed by a flight of steps from the main street of Jerusalem, but in the 11th century, the entrance was moved its south side, where it remains to this day, including he double-doorway, its right section walled up since 1187. Only the original, carved lintels still recorded by Roberts had to be removed after an earthquake in 1927.

4c7e1862-a363-5135-ad52-ffdf9df7a680.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, Marquis of Villa-Huerta
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait shows the elegance and the character of Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta and stepson of the marquis of Cerralbo.
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.third_name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marqués de Villa-Huerta

4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.name: Purse
4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.description: Miser’s purses, also known as ring or string purses, were very popular feminine accessories during the 19th century and even the first decades of the following century. The Cerralbo Museum has a small collection of these kinds of pieces, souvenirs from Istanbul. This Turkish and colourful beadwork one, with its traditional geometric pattern and the promise of a fashionable outfit, would have surely delighted any lady.
4cb2c7b0-e6c5-5421-ba04-8e3b26cad183.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.name: The Miraculous Sea Lady Church
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.description: This small Greek Orthodox Church overlooks the Phoenician sea wall. It is built with Batroun sandstone and using single-barrel vaulting from East to West.
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.history: Although gold icons made by Isaac of Jerusalem in 1863 were found inside this church, its construction date remains unknown.

4e0e7286-5def-51f5-b4c3-162106c6828c.name: Silverware used on the Orient Express
4e0e7286-5def-51f5-b4c3-162106c6828c.description2: After the Crimean War, Ottoman authorities concluded that a railway connecting Europe with Istanbul was necessary. The construction of a new terminal building began on 11 February 1888. The terminal building is one of the most famous examples of European Orientalism, and has influenced the designs of other architects. The Orient Express was the name of a long-distance passenger train service originally operated by the *Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits*. The route passed through Strasbourg, Karlsruhe, Stuttgart, Ulm, and Munich in Germany, Vienna in Austria, Budapest in Hungary, Bucharest in Romania, Rousse and Varna in Bulgaria and ending in Sirkeci.

4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.name: Pair of pistols, a diplomatic present of Sidi Mohammed II, Bey (1855–1859) of Tunis, to Emperor Franz Joseph
4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Arms and Armour
4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.keywords: Tunis; arms; armours; weapons; diplomatic gifts
4f197f6e-373b-5299-bc3c-8c7b6db1240e.description2: This pair of flintlock pistols was ordered by the Bey of Tunis from the French gunsmith Claude Bizouard, who worked in Marseille. This commission showed the growing French influence in Tunisia after the French conquest of Algeria in 1830. In 1857, the Bey of Tunis presented these weapons to Emperor Franz Joseph I.

5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.name: El Sayyid Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889–1983), from 1916 Chief of the Senussi Muslim order
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.author: Giulia Barrera
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.archival: Archivio fotografico, Libia, album 25, “Festeggiamenti per l’arrivo di S.A. l’emiro Senussi a Bengasi (1920)”
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.description2: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.holding_institution_org: Istituto italiano per l’Africa e l’Oriente

en: Del Boca, Angelo, *Gli italiani in Libia*, Milan: Mondadori, 1993.

50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.name: *Monastery on Mount Carmel*
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 241
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places; Biblical archaology
50d50f6e-1e18-535b-a66c-a9263d40ac9e.description2: Another important landmark described in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine is Mount Carmel and its monastery. Again, the history of this site is described in terms of its Biblical and Christian past, as the location of the fight between Elijah and the priests of Baal, and the place where the monastery of the Virgin of Mount Carmel was founded in the 12th century. The description highlights other details about specific places on the mount related to episodes from Elijah’s story, the story of the monastery and the description of the monastery of Mar Eliyas built in 1826. Each naturalistic, archaeological and historical detail (such as the discovery of a small synagogue and a Jewish tomb) is presented in such a way that recalls a continuous connection with the Jewish and Christian past.

52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.name: Vanadinite
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.author: Liliana Póvoas (MUHNAC-UL)
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.keywords: Vanadinite crystals; Apatite group; hexagonal system; vanadium ore; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.description2: Vanadinite crystals on matrix. Vanadinite is a vanadate mineral with the chemical formula Pb5(VO4)3Cl. This mineral species was named Vanadinite (1839) because it contains vanadium. It belongs to the Apatite group of phosphates. Crystals of vanadinite conform to the hexagonal system of symmetry. These Vanadinite crystals are short prismatic, with smooth faces and sharp hedges. Their colour is orange-red and they are nearly opaque. And they present an intense resinous lustre. Vanadinite occurs as a secondary mineral in the oxidized zone of lead-bearing deposits and it is one of the main industrial ores of the element vanadium. This sample has been collected at Mibladen Mine, Midelt, Khénifra Province, Morocco.
52254363-31d0-54f5-bab4-97458eb40b9d.holding_institution_org: Museu Nacional da Historia Natural e da Ciencia (MUHNAC)

52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.name: *The Virgin at the Nile*
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.author: Marina Minozzi
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.keywords: Egyptomania; Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; Egyptology; archaeology; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; exoticism; architectural trends in painting; Italian painters; travel
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.description2: Federico Faruffini made his debut as a painter at the 1856 annual exposition of Brera. In his works the artist breaks away from the academic rule of ‘disegno’, or artistic drawing, and focuses on colour. The painting *The Virgin at the Nile* shows a sacrifice. Numerous study sketches survive. They attest that the artist was well educated on customs, traditions and architecture of ancient Egypt. In the painting the artist proposes the integration of two separate themes through different rendering styles: on the brighter upper part he sets the historic characters and in the lower zone the more narrative one, of obvious academic inspiration. The painting was brought to Paris by the artist after he decided to leave Italy because he was having difficulty finding work. After the artist committed suicide, *The Virgin at the Nile* was on display at the retrospective exhibition in Rome in 1883 where Faruffini’s entire portfolio was reconsidered, and the painting was declared his undiscussed masterpiece.
52a99ada-0675-50d5-a178-836792f337d3.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

52e912d6-db07-5f7b-a1e2-6593559e25f6.name: Illustrated guide and timetable for travelling in the Orient. Featuring description of Constantinople and the most important cities in Turkey, Egypt, Greece, etc.
52e912d6-db07-5f7b-a1e2-6593559e25f6.description2: The growth of tourism entailed the production of travel guides, such as this one, which gave the potential tourist advice for travelling in "the Orient" - here meaning Greece, Turkey and Egypt.  This page provides a timetable for steam boats with timings which coincide with the international train lines, such as the Orient Express.

52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.description2: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.

5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.name: *Illustrated dictionary of Tunisia: the people and things of Tunisia*
5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.description2: Italian immigration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. This is evident from advertisements such as this one, where the headquarters, names and addresses of a Tunis-based firm are Italian.

5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.name: Diadem
5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.description: Joaquin Sorolla travelled with his family to Tetouan in February 1919; there they bought all types of souvenirs of that exotic lands. Thanks to this travel the Sorolla Museum keep a small collection of Berber jewellery. Among the highlights is this headband or diadem, jewellery that represents the typical combination of silver and multiple enamel colours. It would look placed on the front of a woman and is complemented with bracelets, earrings, pins and necklaces, of which the Museum has also other pieces.
5441d082-5cb2-51aa-a412-66acc0afe4b5.author: Covadonga Pitarch
