55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.name: Photograph of a diplomatic visit to England
55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.description: This photograph depicts the diplomatic delegation that accompanied Sultan of Morocco Mulay al-Hasan I’s Ambassador Hajj Muhammad al-Zebdi on an official visit to Britain at the invitation of Queen Victoria.
55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.keywords: Diplomacy; photograph; visual document; international relations; European powers

58ffe3b7-a7c4-59ea-a3f7-15adee4841cf.name: Sword that belonged to Carol of Hohenzollern
58ffe3b7-a7c4-59ea-a3f7-15adee4841cf.description2: In April 1866, Carol of Hohenzollern was elected by plebiscite ruler of the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia. However, according to the Paris Convention of 1858, an act signed by the Ottoman Empire, Russia, Austria, Prussia, France, Great Britain and Sardinia, which established the internal organization of the Principalities, they were supposed to each have their own local prince. So, Carol’s election had to be recognized by the Sublime Porte, the sovereign power, and by the other Great Powers. Following negotiations held at Istanbul, in October sultan Abdul Aziz agreed to give his consent. Carol then travelled to Istanbul, where he was invested as ruler of the Principalities and was given by the sultan five Arabian horses and a sword decorated with 1140 brilliants and 46 diamonds.

5a3f6e57-a4ba-5aea-abeb-7412fd90e2a9.name: The objects found in the tomb of Tutankhamun
5a3f6e57-a4ba-5aea-abeb-7412fd90e2a9.description2: This photo documented items from the Tutankhamun tomb. The Tomb of Tutankhamun was discovered in 1922 in the Valley of the Kings by Egyptologist Howard Carter. The discovery of this tomb caused a worldwide media stir.

5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.name: *The Approach to Nablus (Shechem)*
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.artist: Josiah Wood Whymper (after a pencil drawing by Harry Fenn 1838–1911)
5a482712-4636-5e5b-aa8a-6973d1c66d25.description2: This image shows the approach to Nablus (at the time believed to mark the biblical Shechem, according to the Bible first capital of the Kingdom of Israel and situated in the vicinity of several important Abrahamic sites). The caption further explains that the view is taken through the olive groves on the eastern side of the city, and that 'the gate is shown beneath the minaret'. The artist who created this work, Josiah Wood Whymper, was a British watercolour painter, engraver, and illustrator, who apparently never left Britain, but provided a prolific body of engravings to publishers, in particular the Society for the Promotion of Christian Knowledge. This print originally appeared in Vol. 1, page 243 of Charles William Wilson's  'Pituresque Palestine, Sinai and Egypt', published between 1881 and 1884.

5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.name: The Train Station from Anatolia
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

5dda7ef1-1588-576b-a7a3-a8ad499d04b0.name: Delacroix's journal (volume 3)
5dda7ef1-1588-576b-a7a3-a8ad499d04b0.author: Dalila Orfali
5dda7ef1-1588-576b-a7a3-a8ad499d04b0.artist: Delacroix, E., Flat, P., Piot, R.
5dda7ef1-1588-576b-a7a3-a8ad499d04b0.description2: The library at the Musée National des Beaux-Arts holds 9,000 works on the history of universal art, resting on shelves designed by the Artist Louis Fernez (1900–1984). The 19th century collection contains a series of books on the history of Algeria, including three volumes from the *Journal de Eugène Delacroix*, written during his time in Oran and Algiers in 1832, as well as two books by Fromentin.

601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.name: *Dar al-Baladiyya, Damascus*
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.author: Stefan Weber
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.second_name: City Hall at the new urban centre at Merje Square
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.description2: Built between 1892 to 1894, the Dar al-Baladiyya was a prestigious edifice in stone. With its neo-classical elements and prominent middle projection, it was designed to display the power of the “new” state. The purpose of building the City Hall was functional, since the administrative workload, which rapidly increased after the reforms of the administrative system had to be accommodated.

61490dc8-89a2-5eeb-adc6-a5f3b1bd62aa.name: *His Excellency Mirza Abulhassan Khan, Persian ambassador*
61490dc8-89a2-5eeb-adc6-a5f3b1bd62aa.description2: Mirza Abulhassan Khan was sent to London by the Persian Shah in order to learn English. His visit, in the capacity of ambassador, attracted much attention from various European courts who did not know anything about Persia.

6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.name: Photo of al-Busiri Mosque
6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.keywords: Imam al-Busiri Mosque; Alexandria; Anfushi District
6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.description2: The al-Busiri Mosque was named after the great Imam, famous for writing Sufi poetry about the love of God and in praise of his Prophet Muhammad. The fame of his poem “al-Burda” surpasses that of its writer. The mosque is located in Alexandria, in the Anfushi area in the Gomrok (al-Jumruk) district overlooking the Eastern Harbour, on the *Midan Al-Masajid* (The Square of Mosques). The Square of Mosques is so-named because the area is comprised of a large number of shrines to *Awliya’ Allah* (good people of God), who came to Alexandria during the Ayyubid and Mamluk times. The mosque consists of two separate squares: the mosque courtyard with a water fountain in the middle, surrounded by corridors from all directions; and the second square with the *qibla* wall or *iwan al-qibla*, which leads to the tomb of Imam al-Busiri. Above the tomb is a metal dome and the minaret which takes the shape of an obelisk. The dome and the minaret are in the 19th-century Turkish style.

61ad80a0-d9ba-5d8f-bcc7-7486cbcc59a7.name: Tourists climbing the Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt
61ad80a0-d9ba-5d8f-bcc7-7486cbcc59a7.holder: Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte: Authority for the Archaeological Heritage of Piedmont
61ad80a0-d9ba-5d8f-bcc7-7486cbcc59a7.author: Marcella Trapani
61ad80a0-d9ba-5d8f-bcc7-7486cbcc59a7.copyright: Copyright image: Museo Egizio di Torino - Archivi Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte.
61ad80a0-d9ba-5d8f-bcc7-7486cbcc59a7.description2: Tourists climbing to the great Pyramid in Gaza are a typical subject of the oldest photos taken in Egypt. This picture is of special value for its high quality and early date.

61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.name: Messageries Maritimes's Istanbul-themed posters
61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.description2: *Messageries maritimes* was a French merchant shipping company. When it began, it operated on routes to the Middle East. Its ships were used as troop transports during the Crimean War, and were so helpful for the army that the Emperor gave the company the right to operate on the Bordeaux-Brazil route as thanks. This was the first French transatlantic line equipped with steamers. The following year, the *Société générale maritime* (later called *Compagnie générale transatlantique*) received the North Atlantic lines. From 1871 to 1914 the shipping company, now called *Compagnie des messageries maritimes*, saw its Golden Age.

62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.name: National Museum of Archaeology
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.author: DGPC
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.history: The National Museum of Archaeology was founded in 1893 inside the Monastery of Jerónimos, which is one of the most important testimonies to Portugal’s Great Discoveries. With 120 years of existence, the museum became a reference institution of Portuguese Archaeology having regular contacts with museums, universities and research centers across the globe.
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.keywords: Archaeology; Museum; Rediscovry the past; National Identiity
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.architects: Architects: Master Diogo Boitaca (c.1460–1527), João de Castilho (c.1470–1552), Jerónimo de Ruão (1530–1601)
62681131-068c-54e3-b1f2-e3e7012285ab.description2: The Jerónimos Monastery is one of the most important examples of Manueline architecture. Its church, built in a lengthwise plan to the design of Boitaca, is divided into three naves topped by a flattened vault supported by eight towering octagonal pillars. This system provides a unified and luminous space. The main portal, which also gives access to the cloister, boasts a statuary programme depicting the Nativity. The church’s side portal, by João de Castilho, features sculptural images of the Virgin, the Apostles, Prophets, Doctors of the Church and angels. The museum is located in the monastery’s west wing which held the monks’ dormitories in the past.

6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.name: *The French Colonies. Book 26. M. de Brazza's Exploration 1875–79. His treaty with Makoko.*
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.artist: Engraver: L. Geisler; artist; G. Dascher
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.keywords: Congo; France; colonies; Savorgnan de Brazza
6542d634-c357-5d32-8439-beffa72dfa02.description2: In September 1880, the explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signed a treaty with Makoko, the Chief of the Bateke (Anziku Kingdom) laying out the new borders of the Congo. The French government ratified this treaty in 1882. Savorgnan de Brazza was henceforth put forward by Jules Ferry's government as the perfect example of non-violent victory, contrasting him with England's Henry Morton Stanley, his rival in this region. Savorgnan de Brazza's image as a "civiliser" became a central theme of colonial propaganda, as we can see from this image.

65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.name: Valeria Mengarini Rossetti (the wife of an Italian military officer) visiting Menfi (Egypt), escorted by her brother-in-law Roberto Rossetti (an Italian lawyer who migrated to Egypt)
65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.author: Giulia Barrera
65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.description2:
During the 19th century, the number of Europeans who could engage in leisure travel steadily increased, and tourism began to flourish. Ancient Egypt became an attractive tourist destination for the European elites. Fascination for Egyptian antiquities and the cultural exoticism were sources of interest.  
Near Egyptian ruins, tourist could also enjoy the exotic experience of riding a camel.

65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.name: *Harem*
65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman Empire. This photo of a harem is interesting insofar as it  differs from the mainstream representations of harems in the Western imagination, which were influenced by the painter Gérôme. Indeed, many local customs - both real and imagined - captured the interest of European artists, and their Orientalist art then fuelled both the Western fascination with and revulsion towards the East.

65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.name: Ferdinand I, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollen-Sigmaringen
65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.description2: Street Scene with King Ferdinand of Romania in Vienna. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.

66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.name: *The Egyptian Magician holding a seance with members of the European community in Cairo*
66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
66eb3d81-e848-51c4-9925-a840ecb8f574.description2: Although this is the roughest of drawings, a composition sketch, or simply on the spot note-taking, it is important because it actually shows an Egyptian Magician, Shaykh Abd al-Qadir al-Maghrabi, in action, possibly in Lewis’s house. A séance was held there on the 8th December 1841, according to Sir Gardner Wilkinson who was present. The Shayk is clearly visible in the centre, and the huddled form in front of him indicates the young lad kneeling and staring at the drop of ink in his palm, answering difficult questions put to him by the onlookers. Although they are in Eastern dress, they are identified on an old label as prominent members of the European community in Cairo, including Henry Abbott, Joseph Bonomi and Colonel Barnett, British Consul-General in Egypt.

67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.name: *Souvenir of Algeria*
67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.author: Dalila Orfali
67aa0756-7dec-5fdf-a48c-f7c56bbd3c48.description2: This painting, made during one of the artist's many trips to Algeria, shows the ancient aqueduct of Cherchell. Algeria, for Fromentin, remained and endless source of inspiration to be constantly reinterpreted, as we can see from this painting's slightly personal touch. This famous work was first exhibited at the Salon in 1859, then again in 1874. It belonged to the old Delagrade collection and was published in *La Gazette des Beaux-Arts* in 1859 along with the following commentary: "This group of brightly dressed horsemen, who stand out like rubies against the green hills of the valley under the acqueduct, is above all the work of a colourist artist who has succeeded in uniting science with audacity.".

686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.name: *Arab horseman*
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.author: Dalila Orfali
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.second_name: 1846 sketch for the porait of Ali Ben Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. Currently held in the Musée de Versailles.
686e2212-e7f1-527b-a985-4e1c54e9ef94.description2: This piece, drawn in 1846, is a study for the portrait of 'Ali bin Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. The portrait is currently held in the Musée de Versailles. The artist has concentrated on his posture rather than his face, which is sparse on details. The artist came to Constantine in May 1846 and said: "This is the only truly Arab city left in this country". In 1844 he was summoned by the Bey Ahmed, who he met in France, and was commissioned to paint his portrait on horseback surrounded by his beylical guard. The prints cabinet at the Musée National des Beaux-Arts contains the final sketch for this painting, which was exhibited at the Louvre in 2003.

68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.name: The Damascene Hall
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
68a95c99-7986-5df2-8af1-8a9cc45a55e6.description2: In the eastern part of Wilhelma, towards the R. Neckar, is the Damascene Hall. It is the only one of the historical buildings that was not built by the royal architect Karl Ludwig von Zanth, but, after his death, by Professor Wilhelm Bäumer in 1864. It served Wilhelm I as a building for keeping pheasants and chickens. The name comes from that of the inhabitants of the town of Damascus, which used to be a centre of the Moorish style of building. The Damascene Hall was the only one of the historical buildings at Wilhelma to have survived the war undamaged. Despite this it was still very carefully restored in 1992. A small part of the old Moorish splendour of Wilhelma is to be seen here in the sumptuous ceiling painting, the stucco marble of the walls and the wonderful chandelier.

68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.name: Astronomical instrument: Qiblanuma
69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.keywords: Qiblanuma; Edirnekari technique; lacquer; Turkish Baroque-Rococo; astronomical instrument; pilgrimage
69be0c25-f88f-50e2-b4ee-eb50bcc74ff7.description2: *Qiblanuma*s are portable astronomical instruments that show the direction to the Ka'ba in Mecca, which Muslims face to pray. They remained in use until the late AH 13th / AD 19th century and this example produced in Istanbul was decorated with a lacquering technique known as *Edirnekari*.

6bbbfdcd-9af2-5577-92d7-ef4e14938379.name: *Description de l'Egypte*: frontispiece
6bbbfdcd-9af2-5577-92d7-ef4e14938379.second_name: Taken from *Description de l'Egypte, ou, Recueil des Observations et des Recherches qui ont été faites en Egypte pendant l'Expédition de l'Armée Française*
6bbbfdcd-9af2-5577-92d7-ef4e14938379.description2: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, containing all the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

6c3d3ee7-fba0-54ef-ae3a-b0810a3caeb2.name: A bedouin and his camel/dromedary
6c3d3ee7-fba0-54ef-ae3a-b0810a3caeb2.description2: The bedouin became a symbol of romantic nomadism in the 19th century European imagination. The Zangaki brothers, a pair of Greek photographers working in Egypt, began producing photos of these nomads for Western tourists.

6c58855f-349e-59d4-b95b-645e69fbce46.name: Illustrations from *Voyage en Nubie et en Abyssinie entrepris pour découvrir les sources du Nil*
6c58855f-349e-59d4-b95b-645e69fbce46.description2: People had been trying to find the source of the Nile since antiquity. However, interest in this increased significantly in the early 19th century, and lead to various new scientific observations. These observations were published and illustrated with engravings, which allowed Europeans to better understand the African continent.

6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.name: Pera Palace Hotel
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; hotel; travelling
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.name: Hanging (*sitara*) for the Mosque of the Prophet, Medina al-Munawwarah
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.dates: Hegira mid 13th century / AD mid 19th century
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.materials: Silk, cotton, silver and gilt silver metal thread
6c834b03-f120-537f-ad07-f35c0f191253.description2: The interior walls of the Shrine of the Prophet in the Madina were traditionally honoured with elaborate hangings. During the Ottoman period, it was customary for the Sultan to send hangings for the shrine  on the occasion of his ascension to the throne or when wear and tear demanded them to be replaced. The old  hangings were returned to Istanbul.Judging by their inscriptions, it has been suggested that  black-grounded Ottoman textiles like this one may have been commissioned specifically to cover the tomb of the Prophet (pbuh). In addition to qur'anic inscriptions, the calligraphic panels include a large green medallion with a hadith of the Prophet: ‘ (For) whosoever may visit my grave, my intercession will become an obligation’. Below, elaborate arabesque scrolling surrounds the emblem or tughra of the sultan Abd al-Hamid II (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD), who commissioned this hanging.

6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.name: Pera Palace Hotel
6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; hotel; travelling
6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neoclassical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.name: The Palace of Porto Trade Association Headquarters, the Arabian Room
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.history: During the siege of Porto (1832-33) by Miguelist Army led by absolutist Prince Miguel (1802-66) against the Liberal troops of his brother Prince Pedro (1798-1834), S. Francisco convent was burnt only surviving the church.  Porto Trade Association’s headquarters was erected over these ruins. Queen Maria II issued the law concession letter of 19th June 1841 to order the establishment of the Stock Exchange and the Trial Court. The solemn placing of the first stone took place on 6 October 1842.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.keywords: Oporto; Trade Association; cultural heritage; trade; Queen Maria II; Cabralism
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.architects: Architects: Joaquim da Costa Lima (1840–1860), Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa (1860–1879), Thomaz Augusto Soller (1879–1883), José de Macedo Araújo Júnior (1883–1890), Joel da Silva Pereira (1894–1899) and José Marques da Silva (1889–1910); Painting and sculptures: Luigi Maninin, António Ramalho, António Carneiro, Veloso Salgado, Marques de Oliveira, Soares dos Reis, Eduardo Malta, Teixeira Lopes and Henrique Medina, among others.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.description2: The Arabian Room (1862–1880) is considered as the most emblematic of all the Palace’s rooms, embodying the Neo-Moorish art in Portugal. Inspired by the Palace of Alhambra in Granada combines the Arab ornament grammar and the fertile imagination of the engineer/architect, Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa. The Hall of Nations is decorated with the national shield and the coat of arms of the countries with which Portugal had the closest ties of friendship and trade; consolidating the idea that the greatness of a nation, country or region is not a singular effort, but one of union, strength and the cooperation among people of different nations.

6f32665b-a3e9-5152-9c94-67a17540cfed.name: *Cook*
6f32665b-a3e9-5152-9c94-67a17540cfed.description2: Picture of the Austrian team's Egyptian cook. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.

70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.name: Painting of Vittorio Emanuele II, King of Italy
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.keywords: Oil on canvas; Vittorio Emanuele II
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.description2: This oil on canvas portrait from 1862 depicts the King Vittorio Emanuele II (1861–1878). Fair-skinned with blue eyes and brown hair, the king is dressed in official uniform, with a black jacket and silver buttons and a silver belt. The Ordre du Sang, the Nichan al-Dam and the Annunziata medals are on the left of his chest. A royal red cape is draped over his shoulders, bordered by gold decorations, a white fur collar and lapels embellished with black feathers. A gold crown decorated with red and green strasses sits is on his left, and red curtains with tassels and tiebacks in the same colour form the backdrop. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.name: *Turkish café, Smyrna, 9 November 1837*
70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.second_name: Taken from *Voyage dans la Russie Méridionale et la Crimée* (Traveling in southern Russia and the Crimea)
70ae613d-6258-52dc-8ef3-3c83dcfa4fb0.description2: Denis-Auguste-Marie Raffet (1804–1860), sketcher and painter, travelled to Southern Russia, Crimea and Turkey with the Prince Demidoff in 1837. He brought back with him a few hundred illustrated pages, which were published in *Voyage en Crimée*. This image, depicting a café in Smyrna (Izmir), the "Little Paris" of the Ottoman Empire, is an excellent example of Orientalist drawing.

70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.name: Arabs listening to a story in their camp
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.artist: Engraver: Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet; artist: Horace Vernet
70b73c8c-526f-5ae3-901a-f7ef4dbf4ea8.description2: Horace Vernet (1789–1863), the official painter of both Napoléon III and Louis-Philippe, was tasked with painting the "discovery" and conquest of Algeria. Various images of Algeria were published in the illustrated press in order to acquaint the French with Algeria and feed the narrative of a peaceful conquest. This idyllic painting of a group storytelling was very popular in the Salon des Beaux-Arts in 1834, and was reproduced by the engraver Jean-Pierre Marie Jazet in order to ensure its wider diffusion in the national press.

721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.name: Memorial of Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Islamic Arts Museum
721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.keywords: Sultan Hussein Kamel; Arabian Archeology Museum; Islamic Arts Museum
721353f1-5e28-56da-9787-f6334515d373.description2: The Islamic Arts Museum in Cairo is the biggest Islamic museum in the world, and it encompasses a wide collection of Islamic arts from India, China, the Arab Peninsula, the Levant, Egypt, North Africa and Andalusia. Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Museum in 1916 is considered one of the more important visits received by the Museum.

727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.name: *Interior of a Harem*
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.keywords: costume; coffee; tobacco; rococo; Ottoman Baroque; Orientalism; women; Ottoman interior decoration; fashion
727ea8ec-c6ff-5c30-91b3-9e087af62768.description2: Preziosi probably used models to recreate this harem scene which as an infidel Frank he would not normally be allowed to witness. However, there is nothing in this decorous interior which is impossible or unlikely and it may be based on a visit to the house of one of his Turkish friends. The furniture and fittings show western European influence, particularly in the curious rococo wall bracket and the fringed sofa in place of the traditional raised wooden platform covered with carpets. By the middle of the 19th century French style in interior design was fashionable in Turkey, especially a degenerate form of the rococo. A version of this composition, dated 1852, is much less restrained, its details deliberately pandering to the popular western idea of a harem, based on Arabian Nights imagery.

730d8f3c-b36e-5edb-a16b-a8c763ab2ca1.name: Order of the Osmanie that belonged to Alexandru Ioan Cuza
730d8f3c-b36e-5edb-a16b-a8c763ab2ca1.description2: Alexandru Ioan Cuza, ruler of the United Principalities of Moldova and Wallachia, received the order of Osmanie in June 1864, when he travelled to Istanbul in order to convince the sultan to agree with the changes he planned to make to the Paris Convention of 1858, which was the Principalities’ constitution. In May the modified act was approved by plebiscite in the Principalities and as a consequence a conference of the Guaranteeing Powers was organized in Istanbul. Cuza spent two weeks in Istanbul and had talks with the sultan and the ambassadors of the Guaranteeing Powers. He managed to achieve his goal since on 28 June, the representatives of the Ottoman Empire, France, Great Britain, Prussia, Russia and Sardinia authorized *The Additional Act to the 1858 Convention*.

7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.name: *Ali Bey (Domingo Badia y Leblich), Traveller*
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.description: Ali Bey, a pseudonym used by Domingo Badia (1767–1818), was a Spanish explorer and spy. He travelled to the Ottoman Empire and North Africa under the identity of a Syrian prince. He published his experiences in different books. His travel descriptions had success in Europe and were translated into several languages. The descriptions reveal his admiration and respect for the Arab world.
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.materials: Paper; ink; stipple engraving; pencil-manner engraving
7348dd0d-ce53-5539-9f72-098f52664a78.third_name: *Ali Bei (Domenico Badia y Leblich) celebre viaggiatore*

736d9205-4e1c-5817-bc04-427dac8d02d2.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
736d9205-4e1c-5817-bc04-427dac8d02d2.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

74e93f42-b022-5056-9d51-bed2d2eb0ca5.name: *Map of Algeria's commercial routes to the "Pays des Noirs"* \[Guinea\]
74e93f42-b022-5056-9d51-bed2d2eb0ca5.description2: Having conquered Algeria, France launched several expeditions in order to open up new trade routes from North Africa to Guinea. Europeans had great difficulty in using the internal trade routes, which were controlled by indigenous African kingdoms, so were instead limited to coastal routes.

74f17e3d-8cbd-5078-a0dc-decb3548d54d.name: *Rihlat al-ʿabdari*
74f17e3d-8cbd-5078-a0dc-decb3548d54d.description: A 15th-century manuscript copied in the early 18th century, consisting of one volume of 156 folios, written in the Moroccan calligraphic style known as *Musnad*.
74f17e3d-8cbd-5078-a0dc-decb3548d54d.keywords: Travel; journey; pilgrimage; Islamic pilgrimage; pilgrimage account; Hajj; Mecca; Medina; Holy Places; Moroccan pilgrim; pilgrim; manuscript; copy; manual copying; calligraphy; musnad

757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.name: Hanging (*sitara*) for the Mosque of the Prophet, Medina al-Munawwarah
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.materials: Silk, cotton, silver and silver gilt metal thread
757957ce-46d4-5799-8792-5f05be3e1e3f.description2: This green and black silk textile is richly embroidered with silver and gilt metal threads. The centre displays six cartouches with thuluth inscriptions, followed below by a black niche with a central lamp motif. A border with trefoil scrolling surrounds the central panel. The inscriptions used on this textile clearly indicate that this textile was intended for the Prophet’s Mosque in Madina. The four main cartouches contain verse 56 from chapter 33 (Al-Ahzab) of the Holy Qur’an: ‘Allah sends His Salat (merciful blessings) on the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), and also His angels. O you who believe! Send your Salat on him and greet him with the Islamic way of greeting’. The inscriptions in the two cartouches below state that this curtain was ordered by the Ottoman sultan Abd al-Hamid II (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD) and renewed by Efendi Abbas Hilmi, the last Khedive Pasha of Ottoman Egypt (1291 H/ 1874 AD – 1350 H/ 1931 AD) in 1321 H/ 1903 AD.

75891604-fdb8-540e-af25-a6509a9103f7.name: *Cairo: houses and gardens in the French quarter.* Flaubert in the foreground.
75891604-fdb8-540e-af25-a6509a9103f7.description2: The writer Gustave Flaubert lived in Egypt for three years from 1849 to 1851 with his friend Maxime Du Camp. He saw and experienced many new things during this time, travelling to Egypt, Beirut, Jerusalem and Damascus. Although Gustave Flaubert did not like being photographed, Maxime du Camp was able to take this snap of him in Cairo.

763d6e83-1558-5793-8fef-f63ff6bf1c79.name: Water flask
763d6e83-1558-5793-8fef-f63ff6bf1c79.description2: Flask of zamzam water collected by Sir Richard Francis Burton during his visit in disguise to Mecca. Burton was a diplomat, explorer and author. He published a translation of the *Arabian Nights*.

77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Emperor Franz Joseph
77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.description2: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.

7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.name: *View of Valletta from Fort Manoel (Malta)*
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.author: Marina Minozzi
7a167ce5-50e1-5265-b688-b3c912f172b7.keywords: Historical events in painting; realism; landscape painting; travel; travellers; travelling artist; applied arts; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Ottoman empire; Moldavia; Greece; Malta

7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.name: The Covered Walkway in the Moorish Garden (Wilhelma Park)
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
7c6c4813-f135-5843-8f48-660e13714964.description2:
Planned as a bathhouse by Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1846, the Moorish Villa was then, however, built as living quarters with a glasshouse. It was first intended to be a bathhouse because mineral springs had been discovered in the adjacent Rosenstein Park. Rosenstein Palace was already standing in Rosenstein Park, and served the King as a summer residence.  
The Covered Walkaway marks the perimeter of the Moorish Garden at Wilhelma.

7de42026-ed99-5288-a199-da1cae44d5fc.description2:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an Ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station, he was received by the Mayor of Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the Ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the Ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamonds small box and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.

85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.name: Moorish Kiosk in Linderhof Palace Park
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.type: Pavillion; Park building in Linderhof Palace Park
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.history:
Linderhof Palace Park was laid out from 1870 to 1880 from plans by Carl von Effner. Ludwig II decorated the park and its environs with architectural features conjuring up the world of the Orient, such as the Moorish Kiosk and the Moroccan House, or scenes from Wagner's operas, such as the Venus Grotto. Hunding's Hut and the Gurnemanz Hermitage.  
The Moorish Kiosk was built in 1867 as the Prussian contribution to the World Exhibition in Paris. In 1870 the "railway king" Henry Strousberg bought the pavilion. After Strousberg's bankruptcy, Ludwig II bought the building in 1876 for Linderhof Palace Park and had it rebuilt and reappointed to his specifications.
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.keywords: King Ludwig II; Linderhof Palace; Ettal; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
85842d41-d3a1-5921-ac88-903643f0147a.description2: The Moorish Kiosk is located high above the park on two terrace levels. A colourful, exotic arrangement of palms, pomegranate trees and numerous flowering shrubs extends the foreign atmosphere of the Kiosk outside the walls and also distinguishes its surroundings from the rest of the park. – Between 1972 and 1983 the kiosk was completely restored.

868e1d9c-d782-5ab4-a356-d8e849b96e6c.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
868e1d9c-d782-5ab4-a356-d8e849b96e6c.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.name: *Napoléon II's journey to Algeria, 7 June 1865*

87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.description2: Napoléon III visited Algeria twice during his reign (in 1860 and 1865). It was unusual at this time for the French head of state to travel outside the country, so these visits attracted much attention. They also allowed Napoléon to show how important Algeria was to him. He wanted to judge the complex situation which had been described to him in various reports for himself. A lavish welcome was prepared for him wherever he went during both his visits. This image, for example, shows an arc de triomphe which was erected in his honour at the terminus of a small mining train at Bouhamza.

898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.name: *Head of the Great Sphinx, Pyramids of Geezeh July 17th, 1839*
898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority

898f2296-ee1f-5e48-a6ee-73f0b9a210a9.description2: Roberts depicted the Sphinx some twenty years after Giovanni Battista Caviglia had excavated at Giza in 1817 and had cleared masses of sand away from the monument, which up to that point had been buried right up to its neck. Subsequently, he succeeded in clearing the whole front of the Sphinx. At the point of Roberts’ visit, the sphinx was visible from the top of the head to the floor of the temple between its paws. After its initial discovery, the Sphinx soon became one of the foremost fascinations for early European Egyptologists, including Auguste Mariette, the founder and first director of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, Gaston Maspero, who conducted a survey  of it in 1886, and the British scholar E. A. Wallis Budge.It also proved fascinating for Orientalist artists and artisans all over Europe. In Roberts' artwork, the stone-cut monument is rendered in great detail, carefully recording also the far-reaching damage to the Sphinx’s face, the cause of which had already given rise to much discussion and speculation at the time. The Pyramids in this view are that of Cheops, or the Great Pyramid, seen on the right, and on the left, that of Cephren, also known as the Second Pyramid.

8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.name: Jeita Grotto
8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.description: Covering a span of over 9 kilometres, the Jeita Grotto forms the biggest Middle Eastern karstic cave complex. It consists of two different, but interconnected, caverns shaped over millions of years by the dissolution and accumulation of layers of limestone. The Jeita upper cave is 2,130 metres long, although only one third (750 metres) is open to visitors. The cave contains a variety of stone formations such as stalagmites, stalactites, natural columns, mushrooms, ponds, curtains and draperies. The lower cave is 60 metres beneath the first, and is almost three times as long. The floor of this cave consists of a long underwater river and lake, nicknamed the "Dark Lake". The lower cave is closed during the winter months due to high water levels.
8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
8993cd54-bcab-5bf3-83fb-e37e53bc3db3.history: Although there is evidence the cave was used in antiquity, the modern discovery of the cave is credited to American missionary Reverend William Thomson, who ventured about 50 meters into the cave until reaching the underground river. He realised he had discovered a cave of great importance after firing a shot and hearing the resulting echoes. J. W. Maxwell and H. G. Huxley of the Beirut Water Company and Dr. Daniel Bliss, then president of the Syrian Protestant College (now the American University of Beirut) ventured a kilometre into the cave in two expeditions in 1873 and 1874. American, English and French explorers carried out further expeditions in 1892 and 1940 which brought them to a depth of 1,750 metres. Lebanese explorers pushed even further into the cave in the following decades.

8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.name: ‘Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918)
8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.keywords: 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina; Tunisia
8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.description2: Portrait of 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918). He was born in 1842 in Istanbul. In 1876 he became Sultan and after the lost war with Russia in 1877, he was forced to agree to the 1878 Congress of Berlin. The signatory powers of the congress allowed Austria to occupy Bosnia-Herzegovina, which belonged to the territory of the Ottoman Empire. In 1888 he had to accept the occupation of Tunisia by France. He tried to modernize the Ottoman Empire with the help of Germany, but in 1908 a revolution of Turkish officers forced him to abdicate. He died in 1918 in Istanbul.

8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.name: Portrait of Émile Prisse d'Avennes dressed in an imitation of the local style
8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.description2: The engineer, painter and architect Prisse d'Avennes (1807–1879) lived in Egypt for 20 years, and was to a great extent assimilated into Egyptian society and had adopted many Egyptian customs. Other figures, such as Delacroix in Morocco and Flaubert in Egypt, were also fascinated by the landscapes, knowledge and customs of these countries, which became the inspiration for many of their works, thus initiating the trend of "Orientalist writing".

8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.keywords: Minbar al-Saif; al-Aqsa Mosque; Dome of the Rock; Haram al-Sharif; Jerusalem; Saladin; Burhan al-Din
8b03882d-24a1-5f9c-9159-8596cb391505.description2: This image, etched after having been originally drawn by Samuel Prout after a sketch made on the spot by F. Catherwood, shows the ‘Minbar al-Saif’ of the Al-Aqsa mosque precinct, on the southern side of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, right next to the south gateway to its raised platform.  Originally built by Saladin in the 12th century, it was later restored in the 14th century by Burhan al-Din, whose name is also used to refer to the structure.  It forms an important part of the Haram al-Sharif revered by Muslims. The third-most sacred site in Islam, it marks Islam’s first qibla and the spot from which the Prophet undertook his night journey to heaven. The image was first published in 'Landscape Illustrations of the Bible', consisting of Views of the most remarkable places mentioned in the Old and New Testaments. From original sketches taken on the spot and engraved by W. And E. Finden. With descriptiions by the Rev. Rhomas Hartwell Horne, B.D. In 2 Vols, Vol 1, John Murray and Charles Tilt, London 1836.

Broders' illustrations depicting people show active, elongated figures wearing elegant, contemporary clothes. His posters were simply and boldly lettered identifying the destination, and were supplemented with a brief slogan.

8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd

8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.description2: This oil on canvas by Alexandre Debelle shows Mohamed Sadok Bey seeing off the emperor Napoléon III as he leaves Algiers on 20 September 1860. The bey and the emperor are on horseback, surrounded by their garrisons and local inhabitants in traditional dress. This painting is set in an urban dwelling by the sea, and the tricolour French flag is fluttering above the crowds. The bey is dressed in official uniform, with the Nichan al-Ahd round his next, and the Nichan al-Dam, the diamond-crusted Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (with the eagle of the Second Empire) medals are on the left side of his chest. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.description2: This study consists of a series of sketches depicting various Algerians. The subjects are mostly women, whose faces, wrapped in a traditional *haik*, are particularly interesting. According to experts only two paintings of this kind exist today. Before being acquired by the museum this study belonged to an important collection from the late 19th century. In 2003 it was published in the Australian scholar Roger Benjamin's collection dedicated to Auguste Renoir's Algerian period, *Renoir and Algeria*.

8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.name: *The Sultan receives the prince Ioan I at his palace in Dolmabahce, Istanbul*
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.type: Drawing (after a sketch by Carol Popp de Szathmari)
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.archival: *L'illustration. Journal Universel*, vol. XLIV, nr. 1118, 30 July 1864
8ed8ff70-e171-5817-8b08-6644fc9a000d.description2: In May 1864, prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza dissolved the Parliament and announced his intention of imposing a new constitution (in fact, a modified version of the 1858 Paris Convention, which granted him greater executive powers). Since the Principalities were under Ottoman sovereignty, it was necessary to obtain the sultan’s approval. Therefore, Cuza travelled to Istanbul, where he had several meetings with sultan Abdul Aziz, who eventually recognized the act. Cuza’s visit to Istanbul and its successful outcome were described in an article published on 30 July in the French journal *L'illustration*. The article, written by P. Paget, the journal’s correspondent in Wallachia, was accompanied by a drawing made by Cuza’s court painter, Carol Popp de Szathmar, who depicted one of Cuza’s meetings with the sultan.

8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

The print shows close compositional similarities to an early 19th century drawing by the English officer and artist Charles Hamilton Smith (1776-1859). Smith, although not known to have visited the Arabian peninsula, produced an album of drawings - possibly in turn taken from older engravings - with views from Syria, Persia and Arabia sometime between 1818 and 1846.

91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.keywords: Azurite; carbonate mineral; monoclinic system; copper; pigment; jewellery; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon
91a520f6-9937-54cd-a224-0a3b83e3587f.description2: Two aggregates of azurite prismatic crystals with a radial distribution. Azurite is a copper carbonate mineral, of chemical formula Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2. Its name comes from the antiquity for its deep blue colour after the Arabian azure that came from the Persian lazhward. Azurite crystals conform to the monoclinic system of symmetry. In this sample they are prismatic, opaque and their faces present striations. The lustre is vitreous. Azurite was used as a blue pigment for centuries, providing a wide range of blues. It is also used as jewellery and as an ornamental stone. As a secondary mineral found in the oxidized portions of copper deposits, the presence of Azurite is a good surface indicator of the presence of copper ores. This sample was collected at the Touissit Mine, near Oudja, Morocco.

92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.name: Palais de la Rose
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.history: The Palais de la Rose was built in the late 18th century, within La Manouba's royal gardens. Although originally used as a recreational palace for the Husainid beys, it soon began to receive many famous guests or persons visiting Tunisia, such as Queen Caroline of Brunswick in 1816. During the reign of Ahmed Pacha Bey (1837–1855) the palace became a residence for foreign teachers at the École Militaire du Bardo, among whom was the famous hero of Italian independence, Giuseppe Garibaldi. From 1881, the beginning of the French protectorate in Tunisia, the palace became the occupying army's headquarters. Following independence, the palace was restored and thus regained its original splendour and the became home to the Musée Militaire National.
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.description2: The Palais de la Rose is an example of "Moorish" architecture from Spain and North Africa with Italian influences. Its most notable features are the grand staircase, the great hall surrounded by a marble gallery, and the huge, luxurious courtrooms. It is richly decorated in a variety of styles, with Italian marble in rare colours and an elegant rococo style, as can be seen from the Neapolitan faience pottery, the vaulted ceilings, and the tympanums finely carved from stucco or naqsh hadida in one of the styles popular at the time, such as an eight-point star between two stylised cypress trees. Finally, palace-museum's four great rooms invite its visitors to learn about the history of the Tunisian army from antiquity to the War of Independence.

92dacff0-b9ed-51f4-8929-313eefaa5ba9.keywords: Palmyra; Syria; Palestine; Bedouins; textile; exploration; travel; traveller

From 1832 to 1836 he travelled widely in India, until he returned to Europe.

93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.name: The Moorish Villa (Wilhelma Park)
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
93ae9a92-2eeb-5864-aa3f-f804d80d9877.description2:
The "Moorish Villa" at Wilhelma indicates either the whole construction of the botanical section or its central building. The glasshouses are impressive constructions of glass and cast iron adjoined to the central living quarters already during the reign of Wilhelm I of Württemberg.  
The overall construction accommodate five autonomous plant houses, each of them displaying plants according to a super-ordinate theme. From the northern entrance, one first reaches the Cactus Cupola House, then the room with the Tropical Crop Plants. In the centre there follows the Moorish Villa (central part of the construction), with the famous giant titan plant. The next section is the glasshouse with tropical ferns, and in the final room, also with a glass cupola, the tree ferns.  
In the central room of the Moorish Villa construction there is the Department for Nocturnal Animals with nocturnal birds.

96df24b2-d14d-504f-84ae-d796597c98a1.author: DGPC
96df24b2-d14d-504f-84ae-d796597c98a1.description2: Travelling became a great cultural and social phenomenon with Romanticism. The “Grand Tour” through the countries of the known world, and particularly around the Mediterranean, became a means of developing cultural and social skills. Travel became refined and even a simple journey to the countryside required such accessories as this travel case for meals.

9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.name: *View of Istanbul*
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.description2: Felix Ziem, who incorporated the seasons and the changing light of the sun during the day into Venetian scenes, selected Istanbul – another city intertwined with the sea – as a subject for this particular work. Portraying a quiet village at the shores of the Bosporus and the boats on the sea, the painting is dominated by the golden colour of sunset. Ziem is deemed a particularly successful artist in terms of capturing the reflections of sunlight on the water. Recognizing this feature as Ziem’s forte, Theophile Gautier mentions the effects of the changing light of the sun – as part of the movement in the environment – reflecting on the water as “broken into a thousand fractions”. As in his other works, the figures have been transformed into a few colour stains in the picturesque atmosphere.

9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.name: Photograph showing Khan Antun Bey Square
9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.description2: Pictured here is the Khan at Khan Antoun Bey square. The building housed trading offices on the ground and first floors and foreign consulates on the upper floors. There was also an inner courtyard used for parking the consuls' horse-drawn carriages. It was built in 1853 by Antoun Bey Najjar, a merchant who made his fortune in Constantinople. Located by the port, the construction of this building is a reflection of the increasing importance of trade between Beirut and the West following the redevelopment of the port area in 1841. The khan was an important centre for business and trade, and later served many different functions, housing foreign consulates, Ottoman administrative offices, the postal service, merchants' offices and Beirut's first bank.

9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.name: Siamese diplomatic service
9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.description2: in 1861, Mongkut, the King of Siam, sent a diplomatic service to Paris, not in order to create an alliance, but to preserve their independence by sending messages of good will to various European sovereigns. Napoléon III organised a lavish reception at the Palais Fontainebleau, recalling the Siamese reception which Louis XIV received in 1684. This photo reveals the importance of the Siamese delegation (three ambassadors and ten attachés in their military dress) accompanied by the Abbot Larnaudie, interpreter for the Siamese court.

a104ff6a-9766-59a7-acc1-0e2d2676a230.description: Silver buckle, chiselled with floral and vegetal motifs, and the application, in golden brass, of an eagle and two hands. This kind of motif as a symbolic protection against the evil eye is reminiscent of the beliefs held before the arrival of the Islamic religion. The eagle is considered to be a symbol of power and the open hand is the most powerful protective existing symbol, but equally it symbolises the five fundamental principles of the Islam. In the North of Africa, the jewels that represented the social status of their carriers have turned into accessible adornment to all the social classes, used with protective character, especially against the evil eye. They are also a symbol of the wealth of a woman when she marries.

a15b7e00-538c-5aa8-a826-c4febf856606.description2: Cesare Biseo was a decorator and a realistic painter. He was sent to Egypt in 1870 to decorate the Theatre of the Opera in Cairo, where the painter Stefano Ussi also was working. In 1877 Biseo took part in the diplomatic delegation in Morocco with Ussi and de Amicis. Biseo’s painting *In the Desert* shows an exotic Verismo style of painting and is an example of the high status oriental paintings had in those years with the rise of Italian interests in colonialisation. The painting was bought by the Italian state in 1890 and displayed in the National Gallery of Modern Art of Rome in 1907.

a417f6af-5483-5922-be43-098a03e3261f.name: *Algiers, site of the Lycée*
a417f6af-5483-5922-be43-098a03e3261f.author: Dalila Orfali
a417f6af-5483-5922-be43-098a03e3261f.description2: This building was home to the first French educational institution in Algiers, as indicated by its name "Lycée". It was built on the site of an ancient columbarium, not far from where the deys' tombs had been prior to their demolition and the construction of Bab el-Oued esplanade. It was constructed under the direction of the architect Frédéric Chassériau, although the archaeologist Adrien Berbrugger organised excavations before the works began. Today, it is called Lycée Émir Abdelkader, and remains one of the most important scholarly institutions in the city.

a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.name: Babouches [slippers] given to the King of Italy by an Ambassador from Morocco visiting Italy in 1890
a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography
a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.author: Vito Lattanzi, Giulia Barrera
a46e6bab-37d1-5f3c-a753-4f870c27eaf0.description2:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station he was received by the Mayor or Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the Ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the Ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamond box and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.

a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.name: *The Grand Bazaar*
a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.description2: Amadeo Preziosi often presented genre scenes from Istanbul in his unique style. Specifically, he incorporated diverse scenes from the Bazaar in a number of his paintings. This venue, particular to Istanbul, has been of great interest to western artists, and in Edmondo De Amicis’s words “is not just a building but a town”. The Grand Bazaar, which housed shops for a wide range of commercial goods and catered to almost all of the needs of customers, offered an incredible visual richness and diversity to the western artist. A reflection of this opulence is also evident in Preziosi’s painting, which includes numerous details from daily life.

a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.name: The Moorish Banqueting hall (Wilhelma Park)
a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
a81b5a25-c516-56c6-b670-eb0ae21f4f03.description2:
The Moorish Banqueting Hall was built in 1851 as a place for royal festivities, receptions and balls. The Moorish Villa and Moorish Banqueting Hall were separated by the Moorish Garden and linked to each other by the Covered Walkway.  
Amongst the absolute social highlights were the Stuttgart Imperial Days in September 1853. King Wilhelm I of Württemberg had invited Tsar Alexander II and the French Emperor Napoleon III to a meeting of reconciliation at Wilhelma. In 1944 the Moorish Banqueting Hall was heavily damaged by bombing. In 1961, after much deliberation – controversial as the decision was – the remains were demolished. Today the Aquarium with the Crocodile Hall is standing at the site. One small section of the original façade has survived. It forms the wall at the side of the Aquarium facing the Water Lily Pond.

a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.name: *Athenian Bride*
a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.author: Tsigakou, The Rediscovery of Greece, p.191
a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.description2: Louis Dupré (1789–1837) visited Greece in 1819. He exhibited Greek subjects at the Salons of 1827, 1831, 1833 and 1855. In 1825 he published a set of colored lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyages à Athènes et Constantinople*. Dupré recorded his experiences of travel in the Levant in 1819 mainly through portraits of the people he met. In addition to the lithographs in this book, Dupré also produced loose broadsheet lithographed plates. Many of these are in the possession of the Cabinet des Estampes of the Bibliothèque Nationale. Much has been written on Dupré. *Athenian Bride* depicts the preparations of an Athenian wedding. The bride patiently waits as the groom is ritually shaved.

ac213e50-9aa9-50fe-a88f-16a3840fbce1.name: *Departure of a Caravan to Mecca from Bab el-Nasr Gate, Cairo*
ac213e50-9aa9-50fe-a88f-16a3840fbce1.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
ac213e50-9aa9-50fe-a88f-16a3840fbce1.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
ac213e50-9aa9-50fe-a88f-16a3840fbce1.description2: Traditionally, most Muslim pilgrims went to Makkah on foot as part of a caravan. Cairo was one of the most important starting points for pilgrim caravans, particularly as it dispatched the ceremonial Mahmal, an ornamental litter containing a Qur’an manuscript and ritual hangings for the Holy Places. Traditionally, the Hajj caravan left the city from the Bab al Nasr gate. In order to ensure the caravan's smooth progression, the Amir al-Hajj organised each section and allocated it its correct place within the sequence. The caravan was headed up by bedouin guides, followed by water carriers and important officials. Next came the treasury and precious gifts intended for the Holy Places, carefully shielded by the ruler's special guards and soldiers. Another, well-protected treasury section - this one intended for the upkeep of the caravan itself - followed and, behind it, a numerous array of traders and merchants. The rest of the caravan was made up of the actual pilgrims from all over the region.

ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.name: *The Gate of the Roman*
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.author: Athens 1985, no 205 (F-M Tsigakou)
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.artist: Théodore Achille Louis, Vicomte du Moncel
ac5b0f5f-98d9-556f-869d-b17cc4a654a2.description2: Since King Otto (1833–1863) made efforts to transform immediately ruinous Athens into a European capital worthy of its erstwhile glory, around the mid-nineteenth century spectacular changes were made in the urban planning structure and morphology of the city. A reliable image of Athens at this time is given by Du Moncel in his book *Vues pittoresques des monuments d’Athenes*. This particular representation of Athens is the Roman Agora (Forum Romanum), natural continuation of the ancient Agora, was built c.10BC, the Gate of Athena Archegetis, which is depicted here. In Ottoman times this Roman gate was known as the Pazaroporta (Bazaar Gate), because it was used as the entrance to the bazaar, the commercial centre of Athens, which occupied the area between the Roman Agora and the Library of Hadrian.

ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.name: Quinta da Regaleira
ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.type: Palace and Gardens; Unesco Cultural Heritage Classification
ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.history:
António Augusto Carvalho Monteiro (1848–1920) assisted by Italian architect Luigi Manini conceived The Garden of Quinta da Regaleira as a sacred and symbolic space,  
inspired by the Garden of the Desert de Retz in Marly; Torrigiani Garden in Florence amongst others. The choice of its location in Sintra, in the Monte da Lua, was relevant as a sacred site since the Neolithic, associated with legends and rituals of underground worlds.  
Carvalho Monteiro as a Mason filled his home with various symbolic references namely Christian, pagan, Neo - Templars and classical literature as Dante\`s Divine Comedy. The visiting trail, beyond the ludic aspect aims to recreate the theme of “death and resurrection” like the descent to the darkness before returning to the light.
ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.keywords: Neomanueline; Romanticism; Nature; Garden; Spirituality; Mistery; Alchemy
ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.architects: António Carvalho Monteiro (1848–1920); architect Luigi Manini (1848–1936)
ae264026-52c5-575e-8918-d09df5811c0b.description2: A man of inquiring scientific mind and vast culture, Carvalho Monteiro left imprinted in stone his cosmological vision, a synthesis of the spiritual memory of mankind stemmed in the Portuguese Mythical Tradition.  The art and architecture of the mansion and the chapel, built in neo-Manueline style, were conjugated with other buildings in the bosom of an Edenic garden. A “Philosopher's Dwelling” par excellence, conveying a message adressed to those who are are fit to engage in the Adventure of self-knowledge, Quinta da Regaleira emerges from the Sintra Cultural Landscape as an example of the Total Oeuvre and as expression of a new mythical territory, where Philosophy, Art and Nature come together.

b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.type: Hunting lodge; summer manor; royal villa in the mountains

b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.history: The Turkish Room inside the King's House on the Schachen spreads an Oriental fairytale charm with a gold, blue and red colour combination. The design for the room was based on an engraving by the Englishman Thomas Allom, published in an architectural work on Constantinople. The engraving shows a room built by Sultan Selim III (r. 1789–1807) in the Palace of Eyüb. However, the overall impression created by the furniture and colourfulness derives entirely from contemporary influences.
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.keywords: King Ludwig II; Bavaria; mountain refuge; Schachen; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
b15011a9-1d5f-5210-be56-0a51595a1b75.description2: The King's House, built from plans by Georg Dollmann in 1869 to 1872 on the Schachen Alp near Garmisch-Partenkirchen, was King Ludwig II's mountain refuge. The wooden post-and-infill structure in the form of a Swiss chalet has five living rooms downstairs with cembra wood panelling and a mixture of stylistic elements. The whole of the upper floor, however, is taken up by the "Turkish Hall". With its coloured glass windows, opulently embroidered textiles, peacock feathers and candelabra it reflects the fascination of the king and his contemporaries with the Orient.

b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.name: Steam engine building
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.holder: Prussian Palaces (Stiftung Preussische Schlösser und Gärten Berlin Brandenburg)
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.history:
In October 1842 the steam engine in the "Mosque," which could reach 81.4 horsepower, was inaugurated, allowing jets of water from the great fountain in front of Sanssouci Palace to rise to an impressive 38 meters. By possessing what was the most powerful machine in Prussia at the time, built by the young entrepreneur August Borsig, King Frederick William IV hoped to compete with the technical supremacy of England.  
Although today's supply of water to the fountains in Sanssouci Park is provided by means of modern electrical pumps, a visit to the "Mosque" allows the visitor to experience a technical marvel from days past that is still in operation.
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.keywords: Moorish style; Romanticism; Sanssouci; Potsdam; exoticism; steam engine; steam pumping; Frederick William IV; gardens
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.description2: The Steam Engine Building, located on a bay of the Havel River called the Neustädter Havelbucht, is at once the most charming as well as the most exotic building in Potsdam. Frederick William IV, the "Romantic on the throne," had it built by Ludwig Persius from 1841-1843, "in the style of the Turkish mosques, with a minaret as a smokestack." The building, which could still be seen at that time from Sanssouci Palace, added a picturesque architectural accent to the Potsdam cultural landscape.

b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.name: Haydarpaşa Train Station
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)

b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.description2: In 1871 Sultan Abdülaziz ordered a rail line to be built from Haydarpaşa to İzmit. Haydarpaşa station opened in 1872, and in 1888 the Anatolian Railway (CFOA) took over the line and the station. Since the station was built next to the Bosporus, freight trains would unload at Haydarpaşa and the freight would be transferred to ships. Haydarpaşa was chosen to be the northern terminus of the Baghdad Railway and the Hijaz Railway in 1904 and with rail traffic increasing, a new and larger building was required. The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects; Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu to build the new building. They chose a neo-classical structure and construction started in 1906.

b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.name: Photograph: *A Mohammedan Funeral, Egypt*
b20d222f-63fe-50b9-acfd-a854de63e772.description: Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from a two-dimensional image by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope. The photograph is formed by two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board. Stereographic cards turned into a popular entertainment medium from the late 1880s until 1970, reaching its peak of popularity in the first decade of the twentieth century. The ceremonies of funeral, studied for example by the British anthropologist Edward William Lane around the time of the dating of the photography, are very similar for men and women: the wailing is produced by the family and community, and is accompanied by a series of prayers from the Qur´an and ritual cleansing of the body. In this photography, within this "farewell ceremony" we can distinguish the coffin and the funeral procession, mostly male, who plays different songs and prayers; after the coffin, the procession would be closed for the mourners.

b4f75aa6-644c-5905-aa3f-64df7691791f.description2: This oil on canvas by B. de Boynier shows a Tunisian military parade returning from war in the Crimea, headed by the current bey, Mohamed Pacha, at the gates of the Palais de la Marsa (1856). The Nichan al-Iftikhar can be seen on the bey's chest. Foot soldiers and horsemen, dressed in European style, carry the Tunisian flag. The General Osman is at the head of the horsemen, and the General Rashid, the commanding officer of the Tunisian military expedition to the Crimea, is to the bey's right. Tunisia sent about 14,000 men in support of the Ottomans and their allies during the Crimean war of 1854–1856).

b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.name: *Djouni. The residence of Lady Hester Stanhope*
