b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.keywords: Joun; Lebanon; women; Romanticism; travel; traveller; drawing
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.description2: William Henry Bartlett was a prolific topographical artist who travelled extensively in search of new and interesting subjects for his drawings. He visited North Africa and the Middle East seven times and made several other trips in Britain and Europe, as well as North America. Popular demand for travel books was high during the 1830s and 1840s and Bartlett contributed illustrations to several of them including about a dozen written by himself. His aim as he described it was 'to give lively impressions of actual sights'. Bartlett visited the celebrated Lady Hester Stanhope, a British adventurer and traveller, at her residence in Joun in the Lebanon in June or July of 1834 and produced this watercolour during his visit.

b5c0d18b-e693-55ac-b0f0-5d2195dc1c3e.name: Kaftan
b5c0d18b-e693-55ac-b0f0-5d2195dc1c3e.description: Child's kaftan with *agremán* (tape of braids used as adornment), done in fabric brocade of mauve colour. The brocade is decorated with flower medallions with centres of golden thread. The sleeves are short and straight. The edge of the sleeves and of the whole jacket is edged with dark blue silk tape. The front, sides and shoulders are edged in a golden *agremán*, which ends in a circle. The jacket is lined with white cotton fabric and edged by a red tape. This garment was probably worn by children in the circumcision ceremony ritual. The practice of circumcision in the Islamic world involved a ritual in which the children involved in the ceremony were richly dressed.

b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
b705e8a3-17fc-5217-8640-d86017b77c66.description2: This simple, circular Zamzam bottle has been constructed from copper-alloy sheet and decorated with hammered and incised decoration. A very narrow cylindrical neck gives access to the body of the vessel, and a chain secured to its shoulder allows it to be carried. Every pilgrim to the Holy City of Makkah will make a point of drinking and collecting water from the sacred well of Zamzam, located near the Ka’bah within the precinct of the Holy Mosque at Makkah al Mukarramah. Its never ceasing flow is considered a miracle, and its properties are believed to aid good health and wellbeing. To this day, pilgrims to Makkah make a point of taking as much Zamzam water as they can back with them, not least to distribute it to loved ones and treasured friends in order to allow them to partake in the water's beneficial properties.

b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.name: *The Emperor of Austria ascending the Great Pyramid*
b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.description2: William Simpson wrote in his autobiography: "I went out one day and saw the Emperor of Austria lugged to the top of the Great Pyramid by two Arabs as if he had been only an overland passenger". Many visitors were unceremoniously hauled to the top of the monument by local inhabitants, helping unfit and often overweight tourists to clamber up the huge blocks. Emperor Franz Joseph was one of many European dignitaries in Egypt in November 1869 for the opening of the Suez Canal. Simpson was employed by the Illustrated London News as their "Special Artist". Photography would soon replace such drawings.

b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

b92b2e17-256a-5653-8c8d-8f4555614e91.name: Letter of Sultan Mehmet V to Emperor Karl I
b92b2e17-256a-5653-8c8d-8f4555614e91.keywords: Sultan Mehmet V; Karl I; Emperor Franz Joseph
b92b2e17-256a-5653-8c8d-8f4555614e91.description2: In this letter, Sultan Mehmet V thanks Austrian Emperor Karl I for the conferment of the "Austrian Military Cross" and congratulates him for his succession to the throne. In the same writing, he expresses his condolences for the death of Emperor Franz Joseph.

ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.name: *Port, Beirut*
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.author: Stefan Weber
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.second_name: During the opening of the railway station at the harbour
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.description2: On 19/6/1887, the Ottoman authority gave the concession of the Port to an Ottoman company under the name of "Compagnie du Port, des Quais et des Entrepôts de Beyrouth". The concession was later fortified when the company gained from the Customs the sole rights to store and carry all the transit goods passing through the Customs. Constructions works namely a maritime dam to expand and develop the Port were accomplished and the opening on the occasion of the accomplishment of these works was celebrated by the end of 1894, basins were developed and spread between Ras Al Shamiah and Ras Al Mudawar. It forms the midpoint of three continents: Europe, Asia and Africa, which makes the Port a passage for ship fleets between East and West. During the mid 70's, the Port of Beirut was an important international trading station with the surrounding Arab countries and up until today it has preserved its commercial nature.

bb75e12c-a4e6-5ac9-952c-ce0d0a5fbea2.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
bb75e12c-a4e6-5ac9-952c-ce0d0a5fbea2.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

bcd52ef5-9e05-5700-9c6f-f573e35eebad.name: *The Admiralty*
bcd52ef5-9e05-5700-9c6f-f573e35eebad.author: Dalila Orfali
bcd52ef5-9e05-5700-9c6f-f573e35eebad.description2: The Admiralty is one of the most important places throughout the history of Algiers. It was first invaded by the Spanish, who built the Peñón there, and was then reclaimed by Aroudj. His brother, Kheireddine (Khayr al-Din), later built the jetty which bears his name. The Admiralty housed the Ottoman arsenal, as well as a beautiful fountain which is now listed as a historic monument. Today, it is the seat of the Musée National de la Marine. On the back of the panel an old label indicates that Sintès was considered the "father of Algerian painting".

bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.name: *The Library of Hadrian*
bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.author: Tsigkakou 1981, 200-201
bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.artist: Théodore Achille Louis, Vicomte du Moncel
bd196d3c-3ad7-5a3c-a7bf-f9e67e2fa612.description2: This representation is entitled *Painted Stoa*, referring to the colonnade (stoa) with monumental columns depicted on the right side of the picture. Nineteenth-century visitors to Athens referred to this monument by various names, such as Painted Stoa of Hadrian or Gymnasium, for its true identity was not discovered until after 1884, when systematic excavations commenced in the area of the Roman Agora (Forum Romanum). Recent archaeological investigation shows that this imposing colonnade is part of the propylon of the Library of Hadrian. Depicted at the edge of the propylon-incorporated in two columns- is a small Byzantine church. This is Hagioi Asomatoi sta Skalia (Incorporeal Saints at the Steps) of the eleventh century, and was demolished before the end of the nineteenth century, falling victim to the antiquarian extremism of ‘purifying archaeological sites’. The works of the artist-travellers who flooded into Greece during the nineteenth century are tangible testimonies not only to the illustrious past, but also to the landscape.

en: Tsigakou, Fani-Maria, *The Rediscovery of Greece: Travellers and Painters of the Romantic Era*, London: Thames & Hudson, 1981.

be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.description2: Emperor Franz Joseph visited the Suez Canal on board the Austrian ship, *Elisabeth*. He reached the Egyptian port of Ismilia on 14 Nov 1869 and stayed in Egypt until the 26 Nov 1869. During this trip, he also visited Cairo and Alexandria.

bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.name: *Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey* (1784–1839)
bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece
bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.description2:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.

c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.archival: Thompson, W. c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.keywords: Mount Moriah; Garizim; Messiah; Bible; Jewish; Hebrew; maiuscule; manuscript; Exile to Babilonia; pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; sacred places; travel; book; Ottoman Palestine
c1e7dbd9-cbc7-5538-9374-b4737a990584.description2: This 19th-century photograph, included in an illustrated travel book, shows the Samaritan Pentateuch. The Samaritans are a religious community (today numbering only a few hundred people) born in Palestine from Judaism; nowadays, they live mostly on Mount Garizim (Nablus) and near Tel Aviv. They consider themselves to be the descendants of the ancient Israelites who did not leave Palestine for Babylon. Mount Garizim holds great religious value and is a place of pilgrimage for the Samaritans. The Samaritan Pentateuch is an important religious (and linguistic) symbol for this community. The British Library holds an important manuscript of the Samaritan Pentateuch, copied in Damascus in 1339.

c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.name: *Caiques and Sailboats at the Bosporus*
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.description2: Felix Ziem was able to produce works in many styles such as portraits, still life, genre scenes and historical depictions, though he is primarily renowned as a landscape artist. He was an active member of the Barbizon school, which primarily focused on the depiction of nature. In the painting, Istanbul is represented through a few mosque silhouettes in the background. Nonetheless, as in his Venetian scenes, the painting emphasizes the picturesque union of the city, the sea and human figures, which have been reduced to mere colour stains. Ziem, who produced his own paints from natural pigments, influenced other artists with the use of colour in his paintings. He is known to have used “lapis lazuli” for the dominant blue colour in this painting.

c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.name: Photograph: *Arabic School, Learning the Koran, Egypt*
c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The arrival of Islam to Africa caused the birth of schools where the Qu'ran was taught in Arabic. Probably Islamic education was the first education system introduced in African populations. Islam establishes education as a key priority for children.  
Universities, *madrasas* (organised institutions with different levels for studying Islamic religion), and Qur'anic schools (first education that children receive) are used by Islam as educational institutions and have played an important role in spreading Islamic religious, social, moral and cultural values between African populations.  
In the *madrasas* and Qur'anic schools, the Qur'an is learned and memorised by reading and writing at a wooden table. The memorization of the Qur'an is done by copying the teacher a text written on paper, and later recited aloud until memorised. Students were not allowed to pass to another passage until the current passage had been memorized.
c4179abe-6375-58e2-9109-f22b4b9e5ebd.keywords: Photography; education; Egypt; scenes of life

c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.name: *Encampment of the Awlad Said Mount Sinai 1839*
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.description2: The Awlad Said are a large clan of the Sawalha tribe, traditionally based on Southern Sinai. It was escorts from this tribe that accompanied Roberts during his traversing of the Sinai. This depiction gives a detailed impression of their traditional encampments and tent construction. Situated in a valley sheltered by high, rugged mountain ranges, the encampment consists of severalrows of low, rectangular tent structures with flat roofs. Separating walls and screens within are created by striped, woven textile units. Inhabitants of the camp are seen seated in small groups, engaged in conversation or standing in groups, lances in hand. The men are dressed in headscarfs, gowns and cloaks of varying colour, while the few female figures that appear are cloaked in black abayas, all-enveloping black cloaks. From a ravine in the far background, a long caravan of men and camels approaches the camp.

c833e26b-92ab-57d3-b0cc-19ebfd4b94d8.description2: As photography became more widespread tourists began creating their own photo albums. In this English album of souvenirs, this photo of the chief of the Jewellers Trade Association of Khartoum (Sudan) is accompanied by a flattering commentary on his skill in decorating tea cups.

c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.name: *Top of the garden at Marengo, ancient Marabout*
c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.author: Dalila Orfali
c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.description2: This part of Algiers has a particularly rich history. The painting depicts the famous mausoleum of Sidi Abderrahmane Ettaâlibi ('Abd al-Rahman al-Thalibi) who was a member of one of the most ancient families of Algiers. He was buried here in the 7th century and was made the Patron Saint of Algiers due to his reputation as a wise and knowledgeable man.

c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.name: Photograph: *Music School, Syria*
c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The images taken by the Keystone View Company show very different scenes related to lifestyles and traditions of different continents. In this case, there is a man playing a stringed instrument with a bow, possibly a type of rebec, surrounded by a group of children and two adults, who watch and listen carefully. In Syria, as in many other parts of the world, music has had and still has an important role as a means of transmitting knowledge and to celebrate individual and collective events, and is closely linked to rites, institutions, cultural and ideological activities of different humans. This image illustrates not only the practice of this activity, music, but also the transfer of knowledge from one generation to another; music serves as a vehicle of expression and relationship between members of a society.
c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.keywords: Photography; music; Syria; scenes of life

c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.name: *View of Istanbul*
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.description2: This particular Istanbul painting by Felix Ziem reveals the picturesque aspect of life at sea against the backdrop of the city’s silhouette. The composition of the sailboats and marines in the foreground is balanced by the cityscape with a monumental mosque structure in the background. The artist’s use of vibrant colours and his efforts to capture the shimmering effects of the constant change of light with a fast, dynamic brush stroke technique dominate the painting. This style has led Ziem to be compared with impressionist painters, and even to be regarded as an artist who foreshadowed the emergence of impressionism with his work. The use of brilliant sunlight, which is considered as the major contribution of orientalist painting to European art is evident in the city's cap in the background.

ca166ea6-6764-5d07-b12e-8c86a410ba79.name: Medal of Emperor Franz Joseph I
ca166ea6-6764-5d07-b12e-8c86a410ba79.description2: This medal shows the symbolic figure of faith. The angel on the right side presents the crown of Austria to her. The opposite side of the medal has a portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph. The medal was created in commemoration of Franz Joseph's visit to Jerusalem in November 1869.

cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.name: Fragment of an interior Kiswa Cover for the Ka'ba in Makkah
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Authority
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.dates: Hegira late 12th – early 13th century / AD late 18th – early 19th century
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.materials: Lampas woven, red and beige silk
cba9697e-4726-5cc0-9a64-80be790a931d.description2: For four hundred years, the Ottomans sent money and gifts to Makkah and Medina with the Surre procession. The gifts included covers for the Ka’ba, made in Cairo and Istanbul, which were replaced every year. Old covers were returned to the palace in Istanbul, distributed to the faithful or sometimes reused.Textiles like this one were made in Istanbul and Bursa from the 10th century H/ 16th century to the early 14th century H/ 20th century. Woven in red and beige silk, they were intended for draping either the inner walls of the Ka’bah in Makkah or those of the Tomb of the Prophet in Madina. Their zig-zag design echoes that of the main kiswa but the religious inscriptions vary according to the textiles’ intended use. Here, the combination of texts with their emphasis on the Prophet suggests that this fragment was part of a hanging intended for the Prophet’s tomb chamber, which also houses the cenotaphs of his first two successors, the caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar ibn al Khattab.

cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.name: The Celebration of the Prophet Muhammad in Tangier

cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
cc673275-b5d7-50ff-bc5e-1a4f9c06e998.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. In 1875 Italian King Vittorio Emanuele II sent an embassy to Morocco which included the writer Edmondo De Amicis and the painters Ussi and Cesare Biseo. The innovative international relations policy of the young Sultan Mulay al-Hassan fostered relations with the Italian King. During his trip, Ussi sketched drafts on Arab every-day life scenes which later inspired his larger paintings.

Both buildings were completed in 1573 and richly decorated with tile panels. The palace and the mosque were restored after an earthquake in 1890, and the tile panels were sold all over the world. At least nine identical tympanums are now in American and European museums.

cdc33d9b-33cd-5f2e-9225-8b2a4c860230.description2: The Tomb of Rachel is another sacred religious site described in *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. The place was equally sacred for Jews, Christians and Muslims, but apart from a short reference to the prayers performed by the Muslim and Jews at this site, the description is devoted to finding the correspondence between the existing site and the Biblical story of Rachel. The site is therefore seen as one of the places revealing the main scope and aim of the book: the discovery of the Christian tradition related to the Holy Land.

ce785e40-77c2-5e37-a375-478e1a61faa0.description: This engraving is an example of an illustration travel book in the 19th century. These books offered readers a view of exotic and distant lands through richly detailed illustrations. Thomas Allom (1804–1873), the painter of this engraving, was a topographical illustrator who travelled to East Mediterranean, North Africa and China. Allom was also architect, hence the description of the architectural details in “The interior of a Moorish palace in Alger”.

d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.name: Telegraph transmitter
d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.description2: The primary reasons for the Ottoman Empire adopting the telegram earlier and more easily than railroads were the telegram's convenience and lack of cost. American scientist Lawrence Smith – using tools sent by Samuel Morse – made a successful trial in front of the Sultan Abdulmecid, who was interested in technological innovations and science, and began modernization of the empire. Due to the outbreak of the Crimean War, the first underwater telegraph line was established between Crimea and Istanbul. This telegraph transmitter (1912, Siemens & Halske) was used in Istanbul in World War I.

d3410e10-8985-5cc3-ac90-027e59aa77c9.name: Order of the Medjidie that belonged to Alexandru Ioan Cuza
d3410e10-8985-5cc3-ac90-027e59aa77c9.description2: In January 1859, Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected prince of Moldavia and Wallachia despite the fact that in 1858 the suzerain power (the Ottoman Empire) and the Guaranteeing Powers (Russia, Austria, Prussia, France, Great Britain, Sardinia) had decided that the Principalities could unite, but were to have separate parliaments, governments and rulers. The double election was recognized by the Ottoman Empire in September 1859. The following year, Cuza travelled to Istanbul to introduce himself to the sultan. He crossed the Black Sea on an Ottoman ship sent for him. He had three meetings with the sultan, who decorated him with the order of the Medjidie and offered him a sword adorned with diamonds. One evening he was the sultan’s guest to a play performed in his private theatre at the Dolmabahçe palace.

d40510a8-3d84-5ac4-9290-1028f6789eac.description2: Portrait of the Sultan Abdülaziz. In 1867 the sultan made a trip to Europe. He was invited by Napoleon III to visit the World's Fair Exhibition in Paris. He also visited London and met Emperor Franz Joseph in Vienna.

d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.name: Pair of tables
d467849e-57d5-56af-821f-861425864b86.description: Little tables like these ones had an important place in typical oriental rooms for the tea and coffee, and in *fumoirs* (smoking rooms), masculine intimate spaces that proliferated all around Europe, like the Arab Room in the Cerralbo Museum. These tables decorated with geometrical patterns could have been produced in the East Mediterranean, but more likely is an Indian production for the Arab market. The second one, a two-level table, could have been produced in a south Spain or Morocco workshop.

d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.name: Lady of Harissa
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.description: Harissa is a mountain village in Lebanon. Located 650 metres above sea level, it is home to an important pilgrimage site, the Our Lady of Lebanon statue, which attracts both pilgrims and tourists who want to enjoy the view of Jounieh bay. The statue, which is made of 15 tons of bronze painted white, shows the Virgin Mary with her arms out-stretched. The village itself is 20km north of Beirut, and accessible from the coastal city of Jounieh either by road or by cable car.
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.history: The Our Lady of Lebanon statue was built at the end of the 19th century and inaugurated in 1908. A small chapel occupies the base of the chapel, and a huge Maronite cathedral built of concrete and glass in a modern style stands beside the statue. Being a pilgrimage site, the statue has received many important visitors, such as Pope John Paul II in May 1997 and Pope Benedict XVI in September 2012.

d549811b-c5d8-5fa3-9488-5db916492dba.name: *The Dinner held at Delphi in Honour of the Painter by the Elder of the Village at Chryso*
d549811b-c5d8-5fa3-9488-5db916492dba.author: Tsigakou 1995, 116, fig. 7
d549811b-c5d8-5fa3-9488-5db916492dba.description2: This drawing is almost identical to the plate entitled “Dinner at Crisso in the house of the Bishop of Salona”, which is included in Dodwell’s folio *Views in Greece*, (1821). The accompanying text testifies to the artist’s antiquarianism and his attempt to identify classical customs in 19th century life. *“The Bishop of Salona gave us a favourable opportunity of observing some customs which merit commendation as instances in which classical usages have survived. Before sitting down to dinner and after we rose from table we performed the ancient ceremony of washing the hands. Atin bason is taken round to all the company, the servant holding it on his left arm, while with his right hand he pours water from a pewter vessel on the hands of the washer, having a towel thrown over his shoulder to dry them with. This ceremony is mentioned by Hesiod, by Homer, and other authors…”.*

en: Tsigakou, Fani-Maria, *British Images of Greece from the Benaki Museum Collections*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1995.

Located on Place Ahmad el Bidaoui (formerly Place Admiral Philibert), on the port side of the *Medina*, near the customs premises, the hotel played an important historical role in accommodating both tourists and officials.

d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.name: The Robert Muawad Private Museum
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne, Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.history: The Robert Muawad Private Museum was a private residence in Beirut's Zokak el-Blat neighbourhood that the Lebanese businessman Robert Muawad turned into a museum. It is located in Beirut's central district, and contains a mix of local, Western and orientalist artefacts. The palace itself was built in 1911 near the Grand Serail, and is decorated with wooden panels dating to the 14th to 19th centuries. Muawad acquired this historical state-of-the-art residence to host his precious collection of fine arts and antique pieces.
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.keywords: museum; antiques; art; collection; cultures; traditions; heritage; Palace; Museum; Robert Muawad; Beirut
d8832d40-d884-5998-a0e8-a3f9f85b3dea.description2: The collection, housed in the luxurious Pharaun Palace, contains a vast and rare collection of antiques, books and manuscripts, objets d'art, Byzantine mosaics, Roman marble sculptures, ancient weaponry and treasures such as clocks, carpets, metal work, Chinese and Islamic pottery as well as jewellery and precious stones. The magnificent interior includes original wood panelling dating from the 14th to 19th centuries, and reflects the grand exterior and the palace's setting in expansive and beautiful gardens. The palace was built in the neo-gothic style in 1911 and reflects the Pharaun's infatuation with so-called "Islamic art", especially following his numerous travels to Syria.

d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.name: *Portrait of a Greek Wearing a Fustanela*
d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.author: Tsigakou 1984, 195
d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.description2: It may depict a notable of Aighion, Andreas Londos (1786–1846) who entertained Lord Byron on his first visit to Greece. The picture is similar in style, setting and pose to that entitled ‘Un Grec de Janina’ in Dupré’s *Voyage à Athènes et Constantinople*, 1825. Louis Dupré (1798–1837) was one of the most talented painters who travelled to Greece. He arrived in 1819. The French artist who was an ardent philhellene published in 1825 a set of coloured lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyage a Athènes et Constantinople*.

db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.name: A plan showing the seats assigned to guests at the gala dinner offered by the Italian King in honour of the Ambassador from Morocco, who visited Italy in June 1890
db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.author: Giulia Barrera
db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.archival: ACS, Min. Real Casa, Uff. Prefetto di Palazzo, filza 107, f. 3 "Ambasciata marocchina. Suo arrivo e soggiorno a Roma"
db907e57-774c-5cda-a1a5-d1356aa44b85.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered a gala dinner for him.  
This chart shows that at the gala dinner the Italian King was sitting in front of the Queen. At her right was sitting the Crown Prince and at her left was Ambassador Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi. The Italian Prime Minister and other members of the government participated in the dinner, together with the members of the Ambassador’s escort.

dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.name: *La Mhalla* (painting)
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
dc9bec02-eb7b-5be5-b697-9d2faab3da93.description2: This oil on canvas by Bertrand de Moynier depicts the disembarkment of the *mhalla*, the field army, in the mid-19th century for the collection of taxes. The *mhalla*, a military term, was made up of soldiers, *mamluks*, civil servants, merchants and artisans, which were split into three categories: infantry, cavalry and artillery. This army was supported by informal troops and horsemen from local tribes. The beylical tent has been erected in the centre of the mhalla, next to the service tents for the bey's personnel and the tents for the administrative and fiscal representatives. The future 'Ali Bey III (1882–1902) can be seen in the centre of the painting, in front of the red and green flags.

df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.name: *View of Cairo*
df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.author: Dalila Orfali
df2df39f-10d6-5018-8f8a-0c38e886c096.description2: Émile Bernard is known first and foremost for his friendship with the artist Paul Gaugin within the movement often known as the Pont-Aven school. He is known only secondly as an artist of the symbolist movement, along with Odilon Redon. This painting reveals a little-known aspect of the painter's career, namely that he spent some time in Cairo where he mostly painted cafés and theatres. This Egyptian work by Émile Bernard is therefore rare enough to be considered one of the collection's most important works.

dfe6ce78-8f49-57a2-8d22-f6a5967fc725.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
dfe6ce78-8f49-57a2-8d22-f6a5967fc725.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.name: Palace of Monserrate
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.author: Carlos Marques, Cristina Correia
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.history: The Monserrate estate, known as the Quinta da Boa Vista,  goes back to the 16th century, belonging to the Royal All Saints Hospital as a source of revenue. The name Monserrate comes from the 1540 chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Montserrat. Formerly owned  by Beckford’s, then by the Melo e Castro family, in 1841, at the end of his grand tour, Francis Cook stops in Lisbon and marries the daughter of an English merchant. He discovers Sintra during his honeymoon and fascinated by Monserrate, manages to purchase it and starts its rehabilitation. The ensemble belonged to the Cook family until 1929. In 1947, it is sold to antiques dealer Saul Sárraga who sells in auction the contents of the palace and tries to divide the estate leading to the acquisition by the Portuguese State, in 1949.
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.keywords: Sintra; Romanticism; William Beckford; Neo-Moorish; Eclecticism
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.architects: Architect: James Thomas Knowles; Landscape architect: William Colebrooke Stockdale; Master gardener: Francis James Burt
e06ef895-2b01-5e26-b048-45ebf4f4ecc7.description2:
The Palace of Monserrate is a key example of Portuguese romanticism, due to its eclecticism blending Venetian Gothic influences with those of India and the Moors. The building is a landmark in the landscape, with its distinctive profile punctuated by three towers, perfectly framed with the surrounding gardens.  
The former building’s volumetry, two cylindrical turrets, horizontal galleries and a square-based central turret, the windows with Gothic arches are combined to the 19th century influences of Venetian palaces and a decorative composition of vegetative motifs. The stuccoes of the Corridor of the palace of Monserrate are inspired by the ones of Alhambra Palace in Granada whereby the several columns is thought to recall those of the Hypostyle Hall of the Cordova Mosque.

e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.name: *Jews’ Place of Wailing, Jerusalem*
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis
e18d88ea-cdd3-514a-a77b-17670ead2f02.description2: The wailing wall is situated at the foot of the western side of the Temple Mount/ Haram al-Sharif in Jerusalem, sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims. It has been a site for Jewish prayer and pilgrimage for centuries. From the mid-19th century onwards, several unsuccessful attempts to purchase rights to the wall and its immediate area were made by Jews. With the rise of the Zionist movement in the early 20th century, the wall became a source of friction between the Jewish community and the Muslim religious leadership, who were worried that the wall was being used to further Jewish nationalistic claims to the Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif and Jerusalem.This print first appeared (facing p. 140) in 'Walks about the City and Environs of Jerusalem. And: Forty Days in the Desert on the Track of the Israelites, a publication created in two volumnes by the writer and artist W. H. Bartlett and the engraver Ebenezar Challis. The work, based on Bartlett's visit to Jerusalem in the summer of 1842, was first published in London around 1850 by Arthur Hal, Virtue and Co.

e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.name: Petra
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.type: World Heritage Site; archaeological site; Nabatean city
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.author: Mohammad Najjar
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.history: Petra's history goes back to prehistoric times, but its most famous monuments are from the Hellenistic and Nabataean periods. After the annexation of the Nabataean state by the Romans in 106 AD, Petra became part of the Roman Province of Arabia. The city continued to be important during the Late Antiquity and Islamic periods. Two fortresses were built in the vicinity of Petra during the Crusader period.
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.keywords: Heritage; Nabataean; Roman; Late Antiquity; monuments; the Siq; Burckhardt
e1b84d6c-9cc4-503f-aaf7-19adce734645.description2: Petra is the crown jewel of Jordanian heritage. It has been a World Heritage Site since 1986. The most prominent monuments of Petra are the Siq, the Treasury, the Winged Lions Temple, the Great Temple, Qasr al-Bint Temple, the monastery, the theatre, the church with mosaic floors and many other monuments.

e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.name: Portrait of a lady of the court playing the tambourine
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.keywords: Pierre Desire Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.description2: This painting is one of the four half-length portraits painted by Pierre Désiré Guillemet in 1874-1875 depicting a young woman of the Ottoman Court. Her dress has been emphasized by means of a neutral background. She is wearing a *dört etek* (four-skirted) robe, made of *savai* fabric. Part of her undershirt with embroidered borders is visible from her large sleeves and around the edges of the robe. Her robe has a floral pattern with lively colours and her belt has a clasp with a two large stones in a silver setting. Her chestnut-coloured hair flows down to her shoulder. She wears two strands of pearls around her neck and a gold earing with pearls and gems. On her head she wears a cap of blue fabric decorated with small white flowers, plumes and toile.

e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.name: *Map of the desert between the Nile and the Red Sea, including Mount Zabara \[…\] and the remains of the ancient trade route between Egypt and India*
e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.artist: Author: Frédéric Cailliaud; cartographer: Edme-François Jomard; engraver: Alexandre Blondeau
e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.second_name: Drawn according to M. Caillaud's itinerary, by M. Jomard, and engraved by M. Blondeau.
e4c6d454-9f18-5654-bdf6-7ba2ce34e089.description2: The explorer and naturalist Frédéric Cailliaud made significant contributions to the birth of Egyptology thanks to the hieroglyphic tracings he made during his two trips to Egypt (1815–1818; 1819–1822). Muhammad 'Ali Pasha had tasked him with exploring the banks of the Nile and Nubia, where he discovered the monuments and emerald mines of Mount Zabara, and took several tracings from them, which he brought back to France with him. His observations were compiled and published by E.F. Jomard as a sequel to *l'Expedition d'Egypte*.

e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.name: Mosque of Amir Mundhir al-Tanukhi
e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.author: Jeff El-Msanne
e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.history: The Mosque of Amir Mudhir al-Tanukhi was built in 1620 and is located in today's downtown Beirut. Although it was built during the Ottoman period, the architecture bears more resemblance to the traditional Lebanese style than an Ottoman or even earlier Mamluk style. The courtyard was covered during the restorations following the civil war, in order to shield worshippers from the heat of the sun.
e58ba153-b1b5-50fd-aa8e-53f869209b9a.description2: The mosque's octagonal minaret decorated with *muqarnas* is the only aspect of the structure which resembles a Mamluk architectural style. It also has a courtyard, surrounded by a tall portico with pointed arches resting on eight grey granite columns, taken from pre-existing Roman structures.

e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.name: Model in plaster
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palaces of the Alhambra (Granada, Spain), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architectures and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). This polychrome plaster cast res a window in the Mexnar Palace of Granada (Spain).
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.name: *The daughter of the English ambassador riding in a palanquin*
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.keywords: Fausto Zonaro; Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e80dfa93-78f5-57ec-a258-0a31de9fef63.description2: Until he was appointed as the court painter in 1896, Zonaro was predominantly commissioned by European embassies in Istanbul. In his memoirs, the artist reveals that British Ambassador Sir Philip William Currie (1894-96), who was one of Zonaro’s clients, commissioned a painting depicting his stepdaughter on the palanquin on her way to the church to marry a diplomat. Sir Currie also requested the view of the Golden Horn – as seen from the garden of the embassy – to be included in the background of the painting. The palanquin carriers, two embassy officials smartly dressed in their uniforms and the young woman sitting on the palanquin in her bridal veil, posed for the artist for several days.

e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.name: Arabic eye liner, *kohl* and perfume container
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.author: Huda Kilani
e8fc4581-ee8f-583c-a11e-54b1e44bda1a.description2: Padded bag to hold three small brass bottles of Arab eye-liner, perfumes and essential oils. It was used as a wall decoration. Decorated with silk tassels, glass beads, Egyptian and Ottoman coins. The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to settle in the Jordanian territory for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of the area in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.name: The paved road between Beirut and Damascus
e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.description2: This paved road was constructed between over a period of six years, between 1857 and 1863. It measured six metres in width and facilitated the circulation of horse-drawn carriages owned by the "diligence" transportation company.

e98c61d7-b917-502c-aa3a-342ce91e9d58.name: La mosquée de la maison de Pierre Loti
e98c61d7-b917-502c-aa3a-342ce91e9d58.holder: Mairie de Rochefort, Musée d'Art d'Histoire, Maison de Pierre Loti

ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.name: *Bayt al-Barudi steamship murals, Damascus*
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.author: Stefan Weber
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.second_name: Mural in the main reception hall of the Barudi House at the quarter of Qanawat
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.description2: The steamships are of one of the most important technical innovations in the nineteenth-century, because they introduced new modern possibilities of transport and trade and hence contributed to the economic transformation of the Ottoman Empire. Because of this new transportation, cities on the Euphrates or Tigris experienced drastic changes and flourished even more. This impact lead to numerous depictions of steamships in artwork, such as this mural from Bayt al-Qabbani (Damascus, built at the turn of the 19th/20th century) shows. As symbols of the new time they represent global exchange of goods, ideas and people.

ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.name: *Le consul Joseph Raffo* (painting)
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.author: Bechir Yazidi
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
ea69f41d-1b91-5ee4-8097-8aba9db33c0f.description2: Giuseppe Maria Joseph Raffo, the subject of this painting, was born in Tunis in 1795 and is depicted here in full uniform with the air of an important Turkish dignitary. He entered service as a secretary to Bey Hassine, and later served as Tunisia's Minister for Foreign Affairs under his rule as well as that of his successors, despite being a Sardinian subject all the while. He made a fortune by taking over a tuna farm in the Cap Bon region in the form of private concession. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.name: The Belvedere (Wilhelma Park)
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
eae0553a-c677-57b1-9a70-eda8e6211616.description2: The Belvedere is situated on the Rosenstein slope and, as the name signifies (it is Italian for "lovely view"), it is one of the loveliest viewing spots at Wilhelma. From 1851 onwards it served King Wilhelm I of Württemberg as a place to enjoy the view across to the Burial Chapel on Rotenberg Hill and over the Swabian countryside. The Belvedere forms the upper limit of the Sub Tropics Terraces and also of the entire historical Wilhelma, The pavilion itself is closed to the public, but the view can still be enjoyed.

eaf5a4c2-fc34-59cc-85e1-5bfdbe4b17c3.name: *Falcon chase*
eaf5a4c2-fc34-59cc-85e1-5bfdbe4b17c3.author: Dalila Orfali
eaf5a4c2-fc34-59cc-85e1-5bfdbe4b17c3.second_name: Watercolour sketch for the great painting of the 1863 Salon, for Napoléon III's collection; Sketch for the painting at the Louvre
eaf5a4c2-fc34-59cc-85e1-5bfdbe4b17c3.description2: Fromentin's inspiration for this painting came from the journey he made in 1853 from Médéa to Laghouat, crossing the great expanses of the halfa grass and wormwood deserts. On his way, he came across a spring where grey vultures were drinking.

eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.name: Pena Palace
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.holder: Sintra Parks Monte da Lua, Conservation Company
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.author: Maria Regina Anacleto (Palácio da Pena)
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.history:
The initial small convent of friars Hieronymites rebuilt by King Manuel I (1481-1495), was rather damaged with 1755 earthquake. It was purchased in ruins with the surrounding forest by King Ferdinand II (1838) husband of Queen Maria II (1819-1853), to be adapted as a royal summer residence.  
The convent fascinated the king, namely the hill and the aesthetic enhancement of the ruins as a result of his Germanic origin and of the romanticism in vogue. Firstly the convent’s accommodations around the old cloister were adapted for residential use and the convent’s church became a private chapel. In 1843, a new wing was added with larger rooms and reception hall, such as the Great Hall. German amateur architect Baron von Eschwege carried out the work under the king’s close supervision.
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.keywords: Romantic Period; Sintra; Pena; Palace; Architecture; Neo-Moorish; Neo-Manueline; Eclecticism
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.architects: Architects: Baron of Eschwege (1840–1847), Demetrio Cinnatti, Wenceslau Cifka (1846–1847); Carpenter: Gregório Casimiro; Ceramist: Company Pickman (1846–1847); Designers: Fernando de Saxe-Coburgo (1846–1847), Nicolau Pires (1840), Visconde de Meneses (attr., 1841–1843); Sculptor: Nicolau de Chanterene (attr., 1532); Menuisier: Barbosa e Costa (1846–1847); stoneman: João Henriques (1840–1847), João Luís (16 th cent.); Stained glass artist: Kerner.
eb85ace1-331f-51ea-a2d6-78f331e3d54f.description2: Fernando II conceived a romantic revivalist and eclectic palace, blending Gothic, Manuelin and Arab styles into what became the epitome of the Portuguese Romanticism. The main features are the outside walls crowned by a Neo-Moorish arcade, the Queen’s terrace with arcades in the Arabian style; the entrance gate with a drawbridge, functioning as an “antecamber” that prepares the visitor to understand the portico, the “Triton Arch”, an allegory of the creation of the world, sited in the façade of the new palace. The arch leads to the arcaded courtyard with an Arab inspired ceiling in its passageway. For the façade overlooking the courtyard the king designed a window inspired on the one of the Convento de Cristo (Tomar)  that is now seen as the beginning of the neo-Manueline style.

eba85bbe-07ea-54e1-b12e-dd3f891151d0.name: *Woman taking an afternoon nap*
eba85bbe-07ea-54e1-b12e-dd3f891151d0.author: Dalila Orfali
eba85bbe-07ea-54e1-b12e-dd3f891151d0.description2: Women in Orientalist art were frequently idealised: the theme of the naked, languishing concubine dominated European art throughout the 19th century. Alfred Chataud's work, however, seems to approach the theme with less artificiality, and indeed this watercolour shows a great degree of authenticity in depicting a scene from Algerian women's daily lives in the late 19th century. The painting even seems to resemble Gustave Courbet's *Demoiselles au bords de la Seine*.

edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.name: The Moroccan Embassy in Rome
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.author: Giulia Barrera
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.archival: *La Tribuna illustrata*, a. I, n. 25, 22 June 1890, p. 380.
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.second_name: The Sultan of Morocco’s Ambassador, Haji el Maati Ben-el-Kebir Ben el Madani el Mazamizi during his visit to Italy in 1890
edae7a23-07b5-5d83-9c59-298568ea0cc0.description2:
In June 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent an Ambassador to Italy (Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi), to meet the Italian King and present him with extremely rich gifts.  
The Ambassador was received with the highest honours. He met with the Italian Prime Minister and with the King, who offered him a gala dinner.  
In this picture one can see Morocco’s Ambassador, his interpreter, two Moroccan dignitaries who travelled with him, an Italian diplomat and another Italian high official.

ede894ef-e932-5091-a746-d1686d47ff68.name: Photos of the entrance to the Birds Room, photos of the Birds Room and of the Egyptian Gazelle at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
ede894ef-e932-5091-a746-d1686d47ff68.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)
ede894ef-e932-5091-a746-d1686d47ff68.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

edea7f90-3f66-5675-adbf-cd4fe3995f84.name: Painting, *Diplomatic visit to England*
edea7f90-3f66-5675-adbf-cd4fe3995f84.description: A painting depicting the presentation of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd al-Sadiq al-Rifi, Ambassador to Mulay Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz of Morocco, at the accession of King Edward VII in 1901 that also demonstrates the good relations between Morocco and Great Britain at this time.

eee2b270-70d5-58ca-a544-89ca4bbc9d54.description2: *Armenian Girl* by Frederick Lewis, and important orientalist painter and etcher.

eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.name: Monumental Ensemble of Bussaco
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.type: Civil architecture changing the ancient religious architecture
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.author: Alexandre d'Almeida, Marta Simões
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.history: 1620 - the Barefoot Carmelite created a “Bos Sacrum” in a walled forest of 105 acres, on the Bussaco Mountain, north of Coimbra, supposed to represent “Mount Carmel” and the “Earthly Paradise”. Following the dissolution of the monasteries in 1834 the forest was abandoned. 1850 - plans followed to turn the ancient convent into a royal residence for Queen Maria Pia, with  luxurious landscape intervention by Roda & Figli (Torino) taking place.  Political circumstances interrupted the project that was later commisioned by her grandson King Charles with the construction of the iconic Neo-Manueline castle, from 1888 to 1907, under project of Luigi Manini, as an homage to the Portuguese Age Discovery and the Battle of Bussaco. 1917 it was transformed into the deluxe Bussaco Palace Hotel.
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.keywords: Tourism; Leisure; Trekking; Botanic; Royal Palace; Nature; Natural landscape; Wellington; Romanticism; Jerónimos Monastery; Belém Tower; Burgenromantik; Carmelites; Battle of Bussaco
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.architects: Luigi Manini (scenographer and architect); architects: Nicola Bigaglia, Manuel Joaquim Norte Júnior, José Alexandre Soares, José Paulo dos Santos; tilework: Jorge Colaço; painters: António Ramalho, Veloso Salgado, Carlos Reis, João Vaz e Ernesto Condeixa; sculptors: António Augusto Gonçalves, Costa Mota, Simões de Almeida Sobrinho, João Machado; stonemasons: Bernardo António Figueiredo, João das Neves Machado, Manuel Francisco, António de Sousa Lemos, Manoel Cardoso, José Barata, José Fonseca, António Joaquim, Alberto Caetano, José Ferreira e Anacleto Garcia
eeee249c-f43e-5b78-852f-c10c356bd5fc.description2:
The Bussaco Park and the monastery were created by the Discalced Carmelites (1620–1834). From 1888 to 1930s a new ensemble is erected, with multiple buildings, either close to the former convent, or replacing the convent’s library, kitchen and dining room.  
By mid-19th century the forest is revitalized associated to emergent rituals of tourism, journeys and leisure. The design of Buçaco Palace was commissioned by King Charles to Luigi Manini, scenographer and architect. Later on, Nicola Bigaglia, José Alexandre Soares and Norte Júnior also cooperated, namely in the Casa dos Embrechados, Casa dos Arcos, Casa dos Cedros and Casa dos Brasões. The final result reflects a fragmentary romanticist attitude, deeply marked by revivalism and multiple references to the Portuguese Discoveries.

ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.name: *Sorolla in Tetouan*
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.description:
This picture was taken in Tetouan during a trip of the painter Joaquín Sorolla and his friends to Morocco in 1919. Sorolla's family and friends were portrayed with local people, a highlight of which is the Moor Selam and other characters and exotic animals, such as the monkey. Especially interesting is her daughter Helena who appeared in a Moorish costume.  
This travel appeared in the newspapers El Confidencial and ABC which also published this photograph.  
This family trip brought back memories and objects. The painter's daughter, Helena, had their little Moorish corner on the stairs of the house which is now the Sorolla Museum. A table, a chest, tambourines, fabrics, jewellery were bought back as souvenirs.
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.author: Covadonga Pitarch

f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.name: *The Prayer in the Desert*
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.author: Marina Minozzi
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.keywords: Orientalism; imaginary trips; reinvention; Egyptomania; Egyptology; architectural trends in painting; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
f03672a7-5a8f-5216-8d53-07817c3aa415.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. He developed a model of history painting characterised by a quick application of layers (almost a rough draft) and by a sharp chiaroscuro. In 1875, along with the painter Cesare Biseo, and Edmondo De Amicis, he accompanied an Italian diplomatic delegation to Morocco. At the opening of the Suez Canal the artist went to Egypt and created his first version of *The Prayer in the Desert* which is exhibited at the Accademia di Belle Arti in Florence. From that moment on, Ussi made both history and oriental-themed paintings.

f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.name: *The Great Khan of Damascus*
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.provenance: England; published in Etching depicting *'The Great Khan At Damascus'*, first published in John Carne, *'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c'*, 1836–1838
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.artist: Painted by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by William H, Kelsall
f1948597-53b1-578c-8bd5-dbd5ac4ee6c3.description2: Damascus had long been a major commercial hub in the Middle East, with trading caravans converging on its numerous souqs from all over the Islamic world. Commercial complexes had already flourished in the 18th century and were an integral part of Ottoman modernisation projects in the 19th century. This image gives a wonderful impression of the activities within a traditional Near Eastern khan or market complex in the 19th century. Under high vaulted domes, man and beast are engaged in various activities. Pack animals bring wares or are being unloaded, traders discuss their wares, rest or ponder their accounts. A fountain in the centre provides respite and coolness. On the second floor, figures are visible at the balconies, overlooking the activities below. The print was originally published in Volume I, p. 49, of 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor &c', printed in 3 series over 2 volumes, drawn by William Henry Bartlett and William Purser, engraved by W. Kelsall, with descriptive text by John Carne. Published by Fisher and Son, with series I and II bound together.

f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.name: *View on the Jordan*
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 65
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places
f23c9866-5c58-5675-bd30-f9e664734c96.description2: In the 19th-century United Kingdom, cultural, political and religious interest in the Middle East grew alongside scientific and economic exploration of the area. The creation of the Palestine Exploration Fund and the development of Biblical studies testify to this approach. In addition, the public came into contact with a land that was becoming a myth and a symbol: the Holy Land. Hence the publication of travel or pilgrimage reports, or of books collecting information to be disclosed among the readers, trying to trace some correspondence between existing sites and the those appearing in the Scriptures. These publications offered a sort of virtual journey through the Holy Land and were very often enriched with evocative photographs and illustrations, such as this view on the Jordan river, with all its symbolic meaning.

f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.name: *Interview with Mehemet Ali in his Palace at Alexandria 1839*
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.keywords: Muhammad Ali Pasha; diwan; Thomas Waghorn; Patrick Campbell; Bogosh Bey
f262f19f-c5f9-5c05-bd10-8873d3e30db2.description2: This scene shows Muhammad Ali Pasha, comfortably seated on a diwan with sword and waterpipe by his side, receiving a British Delegation at his palace in Alexandria on May 12th, 1839 - an event at which the artist David Roberts himself was present after receiving an invitation from the British Consul General in Alexandria, Colonel Patrick Campbell, to accompany him to the meeting at the city's Arsenal. On entering the audience room, Roberts noticed the magnificent view of the harbour from the window, and he eternalises this impression at the centre of his composition, accentuating at the same time the separation of the Egyptian ruler and his entourage on the left and the six-strong, British delegation on the right. Campbell is seated closest to the ruler, followed by Thomas Waghorn and David Roberts, eagerly leaning forward to listen and observe. Other identifiable individuals include Bogosh Bey, the Armenian chief minister, standing left of the seated Pasha, Dr Tattam, a Coptic scholar commissioned by the British Museum and Mr Pell. Campbell  was soon to be recalled due to his attempts to influence British politics towards Mehmet Ali, whom he greatly admired.

f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.name: A Woman from Cairo
f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Egypt
f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.description2: This photo from Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist while travelling the world between 1865 through 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.name: *A Turkish Coffee-House, Constantinople*
f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
f2e1525e-6b39-51de-8e19-c3cca74a4562.description2: Preziosi was of noble Maltese birth, but against the wishes of his family rejected their chosen profession of the law to become an artist. From 1842, until his death forty years later, he lived and worked in Istanbul, renowned for his vibrant and evocative images of all the different races and cultures of that most cosmopolitan of cities. He became for a time well-known in Western Europe because many travellers, (including in 1869 the Prince of Wales) took his pictures home as souvenirs of their visit. Demand for his work prompted the publication in Paris in 1858 of a series of lithographs, Stamboul Recollections of Eastern Life.This is a fine example of Preziosi’s keen observation of contemporary Ottoman life, rapidly sketched yet full of accurately depicted detail.

f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.name: *London-Paris-Constantinople* \[…\] *Orient Express. Paris-Munich-Vienna-Budapest-Belgrade & Constantinople: fast and direct service, without your car and without your passport* \[…\] *Winter 1888–89 ...*
f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.description2: Founded in 1872, the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-lits was originally a Belgian company. Its founder (Georges Nagelmackers) had the idea of creating a luxury train line, without the need for changes at each border, in order to allow wealthier tourists a more comfortable journey. The opening of the famous Orient Express between Paris and Constantinople in 1883 was an extremely successful example of this.

f3ed76b1-bbf6-54cf-8522-0f1b9baf22b6.name: Rich drawing
f3ed76b1-bbf6-54cf-8522-0f1b9baf22b6.description2: Portrait of a standing Yezidi woman.

f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.name: Dagger
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.author: Huda Kilani
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.materials: Silver, iron; casting, incised and niello
f918b78f-57d9-5c0d-a75f-075ce7156c35.description2: Silver knife with silver handle and niello decoration on the front; metal on the backside and four Turkish coins along the edge of the sheath; a name (‘Jomaah Ali’) is inscribed on the blade of the dagger. This object is functional and can be used in everyday activities, but at the same time it is a prestigious object that every Bedouin man must have. The most common types of daggers in Jordan are the Yemeni dagger, the Hijazi and other local types.

f939b530-8866-5fba-afa5-e436e2211419.name: Rich drawing
f939b530-8866-5fba-afa5-e436e2211419.description2: Portrait of a standing male Yezidi from Sinjar. Claudius Rich made observations and drawings not only of sites but also of people. Early travellers often studied the customs and costumes of local peoples, as well as drawing landscapes or mapping territories. There was no such thing as a professional archaeologist yet.

fa167dcd-aecd-50c2-9f06-7fb3d8cf9248.name: *Description de L'Egypte: Antiquités Planches*
fa167dcd-aecd-50c2-9f06-7fb3d8cf9248.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. The *Description de l'Égypte* was a series of publications, appearing first in 1809 and continuing until the final volume in 1829, which offered a comprehensive scientific description of ancient and modern Egypt as well as its natural history. It is the collaborative work of about 160 civilian scholars and scientists, known popularly as the savants, who accompanied Napoleon's expedition to Egypt in 1798 to 1801 as part of the French Revolutionary Wars, as well as about 2000 artists and technicians, including 400 engravers, who would later compile it into a full work.

fb46dd86-2d2c-52cf-a5c4-a7d344fc00cc.name: *The Jewish wedding*
fb46dd86-2d2c-52cf-a5c4-a7d344fc00cc.author: Dalila Orfali
fb46dd86-2d2c-52cf-a5c4-a7d344fc00cc.description2: This important painting has a very particular style, and depicts a wedding ceremony in the Jewish community of Tangier, a theme frequently revisited by the artist during his time in Morocco between 1855 and 1870. The Cabinet des Estampes also holds a pen and ink copy. The explosion of colour and the richness of its composition, where the subject is broken down into successive and perfectly coherent sequences, make this one of the most important pieces of Orientalist art. The Cabinet des Estampes at the museum also holds a beautiful pen and ink drawing by the same artist of the last King of Andalucía, Abou 'Abdallah, also known as Boabdil, turning round on his horse to take one last look at his homeland.

fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.name: *The railway*
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.second_name: Part of the rail transport system
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.description2: Epinal prints take their name from the eponymous town in the Vosges region of France. These stencil-coloured lithographies with simple designs became very popular during the 19th century, thanks to their modest price and popular themes. This particular print is aimed at explaining the new railway system to rural communities, by illustrating the different jobs related to this mode of transport (station master, porter), and the types of people interested in faster transportation (soldiers, tourists, merchants). The different classes (from first to third) and their varying levels of comfort are also shown. This helped dispel and ridicule the fear transport had evoked.

fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.name: *The Place du Gouvernement in Algiers*
fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.author: Dalila Orfali
fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.description2: Albert Marquet spent 1904 and 1907 in the company of Fauve, and in 1913 he lived in Tangier with Matisse and Camoin. Seven years later in 1920 he visited Algiers for the first time, and went on to spent a few months there every year henceforth. He also lived in Algiers for the duration of the Second World War. Marquet was friendly with most of the artists from the Algerian school, and exhibited his paintings in galleries in the centre of town. Many of his paintings were on the theme of Algiers' harbour. In 1939, his friends from the Salle Bordes organised his first solo exhibition. His style, which was characterised by the luminosity and clarity he saw in North Africa, was an important early influence on the Algerian painter Mohamed Temam.

fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.name: Saint Louis Capuchin Church
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.description: Saint Louis Capuchin Cathedral is a Latin Catholic cathedral located in downtown Beirut, north of the Grand Serail. The church was built in 1864 by capuchin missionaries and is named after King Louis IX of France. It is recognisable by its sandstone facades, rose-coloured wooden windows, and the new towering bell tower.
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.history: When the capuchin missionaries first arrived in Lebanon in 1628 they worshipped at the old Saint George Church (where today's Maronite cathedral stands) in downtown Beirut. In 1732, they built the first church of their own near today's Riadh al-Solh square, dedicated to King Louis IX of France. In 1868 they relocated to Bab Idris and inaugurated the current cathedral. This cathedral was used for official celebrations during the French Mandate period. The church was raided in December 1975 and was a site of fierce fighting during the Lebanese civil war, during which time it was severely damaged by fire. The cathedral was the first landmark to be rebuilt in Downtown Beirut following the war, and was reopened in 2002.

fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.name: Portrait of the Marquess of Cerralbo in a Turkish Garment
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquise of Cerralbo, shows the playful and aesthetic use of typical Turkish costume in the Abdullah Frères studio, perfect to satisfy the European desire of exoticism.
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.third_name: Retrato de la marquesa de Cerralbo a la turca

fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.name: *Marco Polo in front of the Khan of Tartars*
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.author: Marina Minozzi
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.keywords: Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; travel; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; history painting; neo-Gothic; architectural trends in painting; exoticism; Italian painters; travel
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
fc95a324-d1b6-5cb0-852e-73608ea38c07.description2:
Tranquillo Cremona studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Venice and then at Brera Academy in Milan. He is considered the “grand bohémien of Italian painting”. This painting was the artist’s first public success. He was fascinated by history paintings and Hayez’s manner as shown in his placement of Marco Polo in front of the Khan of Tartars.  
The artist’s hope to join the Italian embassy – which never happened – was the reason for his interest in the oriental theme. In the ideal recreation, oriental ideas, which were internationally shared, are linked to neo-gothic themes which were fashionable in Italy from the beginning of the 19th century.

fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.name: The Welcome to the Italian Delegation in Morocco
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.author: Marina Minozzi
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.keywords: Orientalism; reinvention; historical events in paintings; exoticism; diplomatic mission; Morocco; Mulay al-Hasan; travel; travelling artist; Italian travellers; Italian painters; Edmondo de Amicis; Marocco; travel book
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
fcdce33b-73b5-5f44-b815-567a60b30ab7.description2: Stefano Ussi lived between Florence and Rome and studied at the Academy of Fine Arts of Florence before enrolling as a volunteer in the first Italian War of Independence, during which he was taken prisoner by the Austrian troops. In 1875 he, along with the painter Biseo and the writer De Amicis, followed a diplomatic delegation to Morocco. The painting represents the solemn meeting in Fez between the Alauita sovereign and the Italian delegation from the Consular Office in Tangier. The bright colours and the treatment of the young Sultan appealed to Italians viewers. This episode was masterly described by the writer De Amicis in his book “Marocco” published in 1876.

fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.name: *The interior of Mustapha Pacha's palace*
fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.author: Dalila Orfali
fdf4838a-7764-5f27-afc8-32377c84dfbc.description2: In the early 19th century this palace, located in the Algiers kasbah, housed the collections of the first library museum. It was also the home of one of the regency's most famous deys, Mustapha Pacha, who ordered many of the old town's monuments to be built during his reign. One example of these is the great palace of Menzel el-Mahalla in east Algiers, which was later partly destroyed, with the rest being used as a hospital for the French expeditionary corps. The dey was assassinated in 1805.

fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.name: The Empress visits the Orient
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.keywords: Constantinople; Turkey; religions buildings; Hagia Sophia; Empress Eugénie
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.second_name: *Her Majesty visits the Hagia Sofia in Constantinople*
fe6b786f-510f-5112-b531-2e5e437342ab.description2: The Empress Eugénie (Napoléon III's wife) stopped off in Istanbul on her way to Suez, where she was representing France at the inauguration of the Suez Canal. This visit marked the beginning of improving relations between France and Turkey. Eugénie was received with great respect and visited all the great monuments of the city. A fervent Catholic, she could not resist stopping off at the Hagia Sophia mosque, which had once been an Orthodox cathedral.

ff0f0b5a-89b7-5bab-b342-1924a2ccdcb4.name: Rug
ff0f0b5a-89b7-5bab-b342-1924a2ccdcb4.author: Houria Cherid
ff0f0b5a-89b7-5bab-b342-1924a2ccdcb4.description2: This knotted-pile carpet is an example of a typical Anatolian rug, decorated with a *mihrab*, surrounded by three different borders. It features floral and geometric patterns in red, yellow, green and blue.

ff1cc08e-5e46-58f1-ba2a-f93481917b38.name: Waistcoat (*Yelek*)
ff1cc08e-5e46-58f1-ba2a-f93481917b38.description: This beautiful feminine traditional *yelek* (waistcoat) is a part of a women’s typical dress. The red velvet and the light vegetal pattern embroidery handwork enhance the elegance of the piece. The Marquise of Cerralbo or her daughter would be the probable admirers and purchasers.
ff1cc08e-5e46-58f1-ba2a-f93481917b38.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes

ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.name: *View of Istanbul: the Valide Sultan Mosque and the port*
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.second_name: Taken from the collection *Photographies Positives* by Pascal Sébah
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman capital Constantinople, where he developed a successful trade selling photographs to European tourists and lovers of Orientalism. The great changes Constantinople underwent towards the end of the 19th century are evident in this image. The Valide Sutlan Mosque dominates the Eminönü port, which had become very prosperous during the Ottoman era thanks to active trading with the West. The construction of the Galata bridge, the Orient Express railway line, and the arrival of steam-boats also contributed to its development.
